osaka_menya_tatsu_azuchimachi.notes: [Ramen · light seafood chicken paitan and a fried-chicken set near Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A ten-seat counter near Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2011, with a line most weekday lunchtimes. The house bowl is a chicken paitan seafood ramen (¥1,000) that looks rich but drinks surprisingly light, with a seafood aroma, medium-thick noodles, seared belly and chuck chashu, menma and egg included; the tsukemen (¥1,100) uses thick noodles that take a little longer. The off-script favorite is the "tulip" set (¥1,000), crisp, juicy chicken wings with a soup made from the ramen broth. Free yuzu-pickled daikon sits on the counter; rice is ¥100 now that free lunch rice has ended. It gets hot inside in summer. Cash only; check hours before a weekend visit.

anecdotes.text: "At first glance, it looked more like a rich ramen than a paitan, but when I took a sip, the broth was surprisingly light for a chicken paitan, yet it had a delightful seafood aroma! The medium-thick noodles had a nice bite." — September 2026, chicken paitan seafood ramen ¥1,000.

"You might wonder why a ramen shop serves fried chicken… It's crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside, and the accompanying soup, made with ramen broth, is absolutely fantastic." — September 2026, tulip set ¥1,000.

osaka_tori_soba_kobako_nishihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · clear chicken shoyu and rotating specials by Awaza] A seven-seat counter a minute from Awaza, open since 2016. The tori soba is a clear chicken-bone shoyu, subtly sweet with a clean, sharp edge and a lift of yuzu peel, on medium-thin straight noodles with three kinds of chashu (¥750 at a limited-time price; ¥900 with a runny seasoned egg). There's also a tori paitan. What keeps one regular coming back nine times is the rotating limited menu: a Kochi-style jyanmen with garlic chives, horumon and egg, a chilled tantanmen, the "Kobako-ppo" chilled kombu-style noodles with wasabi, a chashu mazesoba. Add the ¥150 green-onion salt chashu rice at lunch. Service is attentive. Open to 23:00 on weekdays.

anecdotes.text: "The clear broth made from chicken bones and soy sauce has a deep flavor, and the addition of yuzu peel adds a refreshing aroma… The medium-thin noodles have a nice bite and pair well with the two types of chashu—thigh and breast meat." — September 2026, tori soba with seasoned egg ¥900.

"The soup is a soy-based chicken broth with a low viscosity, featuring garlic chives, Horumon, and beaten eggs… This style is inspired by the authentic version from Kochi." — October 2026, limited jyanmen ¥1,100.

osaka_chuka_men_shokudo_kameyoshi_uchiho.notes: [Ramen · a ramen-and-fried-rice lunch counter near Tanimachi 4-chome] An eight-seat lunch-only counter in Uchihonmachi, open since 2011, where the fried rice draws as big a line as the noodles. The classic order is the half-and-half set (¥1,400 with a large fried rice), picking a ramen: the rich kote shiro shoyu one regular always orders, a shio scallop, a spicy miso full of vegetables and minced meat, or dan dan noodles with a subtle Sichuan-pepper note that come with a side of rice. From 13:00 the menu expands to the kuro-tama fried rice, dark-soy and packed with chashu, worth a 20-minute wait to fans. The omelette and seafood fried rices are huge. It's smoky from the woks, and one diner found the service brusque. Lunch Tuesday to Saturday only; cash only.

osaka_menya_bushido_itachibori.notes: [Ramen · samurai-themed black shoyu with garlic and back fat by Awaza] A playful Sengoku-period-themed ramen house near Awaza, open since 2009: you take off your shoes and sit on tatami among samurai decorations, and staff send you off with "have a safe journey." The draw is the black shoyu ramen (¥830–990), which looks inky but tastes sweet-savory, loaded with back fat and minced garlic, stir-fried bean sprouts, cabbage and pork; add garlic and fat free, switch to thick curly noodles free, and size up to 200 g at no charge. There's a seafood black shoyu tsukemen with spice levels named for samurai and shogun, a miso, an abura soba, and a 1.4 kg Samurai ramen challenge. Evenings add Iberico Bellota tsukemen and gyoza. Register on LINE for weekly coupons. One ticket machine; cash only; closed Mondays.

osaka_sushi_kimura_kensuke_higashishinsa.notes: [Sushi · a relaxed one-chef sushi counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A sushi counter where the chef works alone and quietly, a rare place in Minami to order serious sushi à la carte as well as by the course. Start with a platter of six appetizers and about five kinds of sashimi, then nigiri on small, red-and-white-vinegar rice that lets the fish lead: sweet shrimp straight from the tank, chutoro (one regular's pick of the tuna), eel, raw anago with a crunchy bite, standout ikura and a beautifully presented sea urchin. Tamago is Kansai-style, and dessert is a homemade pudding. Diners call the balance of quality and price unusually good for this level. With one chef, order slow dishes early. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Sushi counter run by the owner alone (January 2026 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "This place offers a great balance of quality ingredients, taste, presentation, and price. Since the owner prepares everything… it's best to order time-consuming dishes with some patience in mind." — January 2026, fifth visit.
"The sweet shrimp was incredibly fresh, taken straight from the tank, and had a delightful, firm texture. The medium fatty tuna, eel, and sea urchin were all of high quality." — January 2026.

osaka_kushiage_harusai_namba.notes: [Japanese · a quiet nine-seat kushiage counter by Namba Station] A small second-floor counter a minute from Namba exit 13, open since 2024 in a quieter corner of Namba, good for an unhurried dinner or a low-key business meal. The owner-chef is Vietnamese, and the course ends with a Japanese-style pho. The Harusai course (about ¥5,000) brings 12 of the chef's skewers, classics and seasonal ones, fried to order and handed over one at a time; details like asparagus cut into easy bites show the care. Add a quail egg if you have room. It ends unusually with a Japanese-style pho and ice cream. The draft beer is poured with real attention to the foam. The owner-chef is friendly and creative, and staff are attentive. Open for lunch too.

chef_bio.background: Kushiage counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews). The owner-chef is Vietnamese, and the course ends with a Japanese-style pho (July 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "This course allows you to enjoy 12 of the restaurant's signature skewers, ranging from classic favorites to seasonal flavors, all selected by the chef… for dessert, we had Japanese-style pho and ice cream." — August 2026, Harusai course.
"The freshly fried kushi-katsu is served one by one, and the asparagus kushi-katsu is cut into easy-to-eat pieces, showcasing the care put into each dish." — August 2026.

Courses need a reservation. Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_sennichimae_ueda_shoten.notes: [Japanese · game-meat yakiniku of deer, bear and boar in Sennichimae] A retro-modern yakiniku room near Nippombashi, sister to the Ueda Shoten in Harinakano, that grills wild game rather than beef. The list depends on the season and the hunt: Ezo deer tataki and meaty ribs, crunchy Japanese deer tongue and heart, black bear thigh and sweet bear belly, wild boar loin, belly and top sirloin, and badger now and then. Diners are struck by how little gaminess there is. The ¥11,000 course (book ahead) opens with a small boar hot pot before the grill. Staff explain each cut while grilling, and service is slow when one person is working the room, so give it time. Many cuts sell out. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Game-meat yakiniku, sister shop of Ueda Shoten in Harinakano (July 2025 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.specialty: Game meat: deer, bear and wild boar.

anecdotes.text: "The Ezo deer tataki was tender and could easily be mistaken for beef. The black bear thigh was satisfying and had no gamey taste… The Japanese deer tongue and heart were far more delicious than beef." — March 2025.
"The bear belly was my first experience, and it was sweet and delicious. The Ezo deer ribs were firm and meaty, while the Japanese deer tongue had a nice crunch." — June 2026.

Items sell out by evening (September 2026). Cards, e-money and PayPay accepted (Tabelog); one October 2026 visit was cash and PayPay only during a card-processor outage.
osaka_angetsu_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese sweets · a wagashi house since 1868, known for chestnut steamed yokan] A long-established wagashi shop in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, dating to 1868 and picked for Tabelog's wagashi and sweets 100 lists, with a calm, old-fashioned front and a small sweets café inside. The star is the autumn kuri mushi yokan, red-bean steamed yokan packed with moist chestnuts and only gently sweet, sold whole (about ¥6,000) or half (about ¥3,000); there's a white-bean version too. The monaka is the most popular item and sells out first; in summer the mizu yokan and mizu manju are smooth and refined. Go early, as much is gone by late afternoon. It works as well for gifts as for an afternoon treat. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Wagashi maker (official site angetsu.co.jp, as 御菓子司 庵月堂); Tabelog Wagashi WEST 100 2023 and 2026, Sweets WEST 100 2019.

anecdotes.text: "You can see from the cross-section of the yokan that it is packed with chestnuts. When you take a bite, the red bean yokan has a chewy texture, while the chestnuts are crunchy and moist, delivering a strong chestnut flavor!" — October 2026, kuri mushi yokan.
"I purchased the remaining Mizumanju for JPY 1836… smooth with a refined sweetness and absolutely delicious." — September 2026.

osaka_nikunabetei_higashishinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork, chicken, fish balls and mentaiko.
osaka_nikunabetei_higashishinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 18:00–01:00; Sat, Sun and holidays 17:00–01:00; no regular holidays; until sold out (Tabelog, staff-maintained). All-you-can-drink ¥1,500 (September 2026). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_nikunabetei_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · mentaiko-and-tororo hot pot to 1 am in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm hot-pot izakaya in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2021 and featured on TV, open until 01:00 every night. The signature is the Hakata mentaiko tororo nabe: pork belly, chicken, fish balls and tofu in a good broth, crowned at the table with a heap of creamy grated yam and salty, spicy mentaiko, then finished as a cheese risotto. Sides are drinking food with flair: avocado yukke, a theatrically long toro-taku roll wrapped in thick nori, potato salad with truffle flakes, fresh oysters. All-you-can-drink is ¥1,500, so three drinks or more makes it worth it; one table spent just over ¥6,000 each. Staff finish the pot for you. A second branch, Bettei, is upstairs.

chef_bio.background: Hot-pot izakaya with a Bettei branch upstairs (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The Hakata Mentaiko Tororo Nabe had a stunning appearance with plenty of tororo and mentaiko on top! The creaminess of the tororo combined perfectly with the saltiness and umami of the mentaiko." — August 2026.

"The hot pot ingredients included not only the pork belly… but also chicken, fish balls, and tofu… the total bill was just over JPY 6000 per person. Since the all-you-can-drink option was JPY 1500, it's definitely worth it." — September 2026.

osaka_chuka_soba_uemachi.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog 100 Kadoya-style tsukemen and shoyu near Tanimachi 6-chome] An eight-seat counter near Tanimachi 6-chome, open since 2012 and on Tabelog's ramen 100 every year since 2018, often described as an original take on the Kadoya Shokudo style. The owner trained at Kadoya Shokudo. Many diners order the tsukemen (¥1,450): glossy, smooth whole-grain flat noodles worth tasting plain, and a dip that balances soy with sweetness, gentle heat and acidity, with three kinds of well-cooked chashu; one regular has been 63 times. The shoyu chuka soba is a sharp soy in a clear, clean broth, salty to some. There's a mazesoba and limited chicken-and-pork bowls. Expect 10 to 30 minutes in line at lunch. One diner heard a move is coming, so check X before going. Closed Mondays; cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter in the Kadoya Shokudo style (2026 reviews); Tabelog Ramen WEST 100 2018–2022, OSAKA 100 2023–2025. The owner trained at Kadoya Shokudo (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The glossy, smooth, whole grain flat noodles are a delight to eat, making you want to enjoy them on their own… When dipped in the broth, they have a subtle acidity that adds a touch of elegance. The three types of chashu… are well-cooked and flavorful." — October 2026, tsukemen ¥1,450.
"The dipping sauce combined the umami of soy sauce with a pleasant acidity and a hint of spiciness, creating a refreshing yet deep taste." — October 2026.

osaka_ramen_tsuji_yariyamachi.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog 100 frothy chicken paitan by Tanimachi 4-chome] A small, clean counter two minutes from Tanimachi 4-chome, open since 2016 and on Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 from 2023 to 2025, with a line from opening most days. The chicken paitan is refined rather than heavy, frothy and free of chicken funk, in shio or shoyu, on thin, chewy noodles, with moist low-temperature pork and chicken chashu and a sharp accent of purple onion. The special adds Kirishima black pork and chopped pig's trotters that melt into the soup and make it much richer; the semi-special shio is ¥1,550. Get the chashu rice bowl with its deep-orange egg yolk. Limited bowls appear on social media, such as a sour-spicy jangmen best with horumon. Many overseas visitors; PayPay accepted. Open daily.

chef_bio.background: Chicken paitan ramen counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained); Tabelog Ramen WEST 100 2019, OSAKA 100 2023–2025.
chef_bio.specialty: Chicken paitan; special with pig's trotters.

anecdotes.text: "The low-temperature cooked pork and chicken chashu are moist and juicy, with finely chopped purple onions adding a perfect accent. The broth is surprisingly not too rich and has no chicken odor. The noodles are thin but have a chewy texture." — October 2026, semi-special shio ¥1,550.
"The chicken paitan was refined and elegant… Once the chopped pig's trotters melt into the broth, it becomes incredibly rich and flavorful." — October 2026, special shoyu.

osaka_kai_to_jidori_choro_uchihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · clam and jidori clear ramen with a butter-risotto finish near Tanimachi 4-chome] A calm, roomy second-floor ramen shop in a building of eateries near Tanimachi 4-chome, open since 2021, easy to walk into alone. The Choro raa men (¥950) is a clear broth of clam and jidori chicken with strong umami and an elegant, gentle finish, in original shio (the staff's suggestion) or shellfish shoyu; pick melt-soft braised pork or rare chashu, and regular or smooth whole-grain noodles. At lunch the bigger "Choro-mori" portion and a small rice are free. Half the fun is the self-serve butter, grilled nori and Okuizumo sansho: add them midway, then drop the rice, the rest of the egg and a pat of butter into the broth for a risotto. Those wanting a big punch may find it subtle. Open daily; cards accepted.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (official site j-choro.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.specialty: Clam and jidori chicken clear ramen.

anecdotes.text: "When the ramen was served, the clear broth released a delightful aroma of shellfish that whetted my appetite… For the finale, I took the half-eaten soft-boiled egg and broth, added the rice and butter, and topped it off with a sheet of grilled nori, transforming it into a risotto-style dish." — October 2026, special Choro ramen.

"The clear broth was served in a white bowl, beautifully garnished with large chashu slices, tender menma, and vibrant kaiware sprouts. Upon tasting, the broth had a strong umami flavor, presenting a refined and gentle taste overall." — October 2026, Choro raa men ¥950.

osaka_jinsei_yumeji_tokumen_tokuimachi.notes: [Ramen · a seafood-only chuka soba with house noodles near Tanimachi 4-chome] A cozy, wood-fronted nine-seat counter near Tanimachi 4-chome, open since 2015 and lunch only, whose soup uses no meat stock and no chemical seasonings. The chuka soba (¥1,000) is a deep, slightly oily broth of niboshi, katsuobushi and kombu; choose rich or light soy (rich is the punchier pick). House-made medium-thin noodles, flecked with whole wheat, pick up the broth well, and the two rare chashu (beef chuck roll and chicken breast) are tender. For something bigger, one regular swears by the mazesoba, oyster with nori or horumon with sweet-spicy colon (¥1,400), finished with rice like a risotto. The owner is attentive. One diner found the light version unremarkable. Lunch Monday to Saturday, until sold out.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter with a seafood-only, additive-free soup and house noodles (Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seafood broth without meat stock; no chemical seasonings; house-made noodles (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The piping hot broth had a slight oiliness, with a harmonious blend of niboshi (dried sardines) and katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes), supported by kombu kelp, creating a rich and thick base… The homemade noodles, which are almost straight and medium-thin, were smooth." — August 2026, chuka soba ¥1,000, rich soy.

"This time, I ordered the oyster mazesoba. The seaweed adds a nice accent and enhances the ocean flavor. It's rich but incredibly delicious. At the end, I added rice, and it felt like a risotto." — April 2026.

osaka_chuka_soba_yairotei_tanimachi.notes: [Ramen · very thin noodles in shoyu or porcini shio by Tanimachi 4-chome] A bright, clean nine-seat counter a minute from Tanimachi 4-chome, open since 2023 and open daily, with neatly folded, very thin straight noodles that fans come back for. The shoyu chuka soba (¥900) is a chicken broth with a savory, slightly sweet soy; the special (¥1,350) adds tender low-temperature pork and chicken chashu, an egg and fried green onion. The shio is the one to try if soy is too strong for you: a golden broth deepened with porcini and Okinawan salt under large slices of rare chashu. Don't skip the aedama (¥350), a second round of dressed noodles with a seasoning powder, eaten as is and then dipped in the soup. Reactions vary: one diner found the shoyu overpowering and an egg forgotten. Lunch fills after noon. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Chuka soba on very thin noodles; aedama.

anecdotes.text: "The noodles are extremely thin, resembling the straight noodles used in tonkotsu ramen. They soak up the broth beautifully… The toppings include low-temperature cooked pork chashu, chicken chashu, a soft-boiled egg, fried green onions, and nori." — October 2026, special shoyu ¥1,350.
"Taking a sip of the broth, I was greeted with a deep richness and refined umami from the porcini mushrooms and special Okinawan salt." — October 2026, shio chuka soba.

osaka_mentomi_tenyo_taishobashi.notes: [Ramen · garlic tonkotsu shoyu until 5 am by Taisho and Kyocera Dome] A lively local garlic-ramen shop under a yellow sign a few minutes from Taisho Station, open until 05:00 and busy after Kyocera Dome events. The base ramen (¥1,100) is a surprisingly light tonkotsu-shoyu, made, the shop says, from pork head, chicken feet, pork belly and vegetables; it comes alive when you load on the fresh minced garlic, adjustable when you order. Medium-thick curly noodles hold it well, and the thick pork-belly chashu melts. Add set A (+¥350) for stir-fried takana, kimchi and rice. Variations include a miso, a hyaku-negi bowl heaped with Kujo green onion, a tangy-spicy "W vinegar" ramen, and tsukemen. The same garlic-ramen name has a Shinmachi shop in this guide. Staff are friendly. Smoking allowed; AMEX only for cards.

chef_bio.background: Garlic ramen shop (official site tenyou.jp; Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: House tonkotsu of 40% pork head, 40% chicken feet, 10% pork belly and 10% vegetables (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The tonkotsu-based broth is surprisingly mild and not overly rich, offering a light texture. However, the addition of robust garlic gives it a powerful punch… The medium-thick curly noodles hold the broth well." — October 2026, ramen ¥1,100.
"The ramen itself lacks a bit of punch. However, when you add a generous amount of the separately served minced garlic, the flavor explodes." — October 2026.

osaka_chuka_soba_hanakyo_taisho.notes: [Ramen · rich back-fat tonkotsu shoyu by JR Taisho Station] A small ramen shop seconds from JR Taisho, open here since 2017 and carrying on a bowl that late-night drinkers once loved at its former Kyobashi shop, with Orix memorabilia and signatures on the walls. The chuka soba is a thick soy tonkotsu glossed with back fat and a strong pork-bone aroma, nostalgic and indulgent but with a clean finish; the rich ajitama version is ¥1,000, and the special adds thick chashu. Choose thin straight noodles or thicker Chinese-style noodles; large is free. Add the moyashi chashu rice bowl (¥360). The pork aroma isn't for everyone, and one diner had cleanliness concerns. Handy before a Kyocera Dome event. Open to 23:00; closed Mondays.

"It was a thick soy sauce tonkotsu ramen topped with thick chashu, a soft-boiled egg, and menma. While it was quite rich, the aftertaste was pleasant… large size is free, and you can choose between thin noodles and Chinese-style noodles." — September 2026, special rich chuka soba.

osaka_chonmage_shokudo_ramenbu_uehonmach.notes: [Ramen · a ramen-and-set-meal diner by Tanimachi 6-chome] A casual ramen diner near Tanimachi 6-chome, open since 2012, where you can have a quick lunch set or settle in for beer, gyoza and fries at night, with the TV on. The lunch ramen set (¥990) pairs a rich soy tonkotsu with gyoza and rice. The spicy miso (¥1,140 with rice) is mild and creamy rather than fiery, with crunchy mizuna. There are chicken paitan bowls in shio or shoyu, rich and punchy, and a garlic-butter chicken ramen with thin noodles as a ¥1,600 set. Smaller mini-ramen sets suit lighter appetites, and garlic powder on the counter perks things up. One diner found the noodles a little soft. Short waits at lunch; open late most nights.

"The rich chicken broth infused with garlic butter paired perfectly with the thin noodles, making it delicious." — September 2026, garlic butter ramen set ¥1,600.

osaka_shinsaibashi_sushi_en.notes: [Sushi · sushi and tempura in one omakase, drinks included, in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A seven-seat wooden counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since October 2025, whose omakase combines Edomae sushi with fresh tempura and makes the price easy: ¥15,000 with free-flow soft drinks, or ¥18,000 with alcohol. The chef has more than 25 years of experience. Expect a clear hamo soup, sawara sashimi, a striking mackerel "prosciutto," then crisp tempura of abalone, anago or nodoguro and maitake with yuzu-kosho salt, and a chawanmushi topped with Hokkaido sea urchin, before nigiri on lightly pressed red-vinegar rice, each fish prepared its own way and served at the right temperature: otoro, akami, generous uni. Diners note the knife work at the counter and a calm atmosphere for special occasions. Book ahead.

chef_bio.background: Sushi-and-tempura omakase counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews). The chef has more than 25 years of experience (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The sushi is made with red vinegar rice and seasonal fish, prepared in various styles such as marinated, seared, steamed, and boiled… The abalone tempura has a light batter that gives way to a delightful crunch." — September 2026.

"The standout for me was the mackerel prosciutto… As for the sushi, each piece was served at the appropriate temperature after checking the temperature of the ingredients." — September 2026, ¥15,000 course.

osaka_yakiniku_yacchan_namba.hours_raw: Daily 17:00–24:00 (Tabelog, staff-maintained). Reservations on Tabelog recommended; the counter fills (May 2026). Smoking allowed. Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Free Wi-Fi.
osaka_yakiniku_yacchan_namba.notes: [Yakiniku · thick-cut beef sliced to order at a Namba counter] A lively 14-seat yakiniku counter a minute from Namba Station, open since 2024, where staff cut the meat to order and season it in front of you. The thick-cut series is the reason to come: premium salted tongue with lemon and a thick outside skirt with wasabi soy, juicy and generously portioned. Start with kakuteki or cucumber kimchi, order rice even if you usually don't, and finish with a soupy curry ochazuke or curry zosui. The ¥5,000 recommended course is good value. One diner found the menu a little limited. The counter fills quickly, so book on Tabelog. Smoking allowed; open nightly until midnight.

chef_bio.background: Counter yakiniku; reviewers mention a Kyobashi shop of the same name (March 2026; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The highlight here is definitely the 'Thick Cut' series. The thick-cut tongue and outside skirt are particularly impressive, and when grilled to perfection, they burst with juicy flavors." — June 2026.
"The style here involves cutting the meat right in front of you and seasoning it on the spot before serving. The meat was fresh, and the seasoning was exquisite." — August 2026.

osaka_shunko_ryoribito_yuu_dotonbori.notes: [Japanese · a one-chef counter kappo hidden under Dotonbori] A ten-seat counter in a basement in the heart of Dotonbori, open since 2013 and run by one chef, with a back door onto a terrace over the Dotonbori River. The cooking is creative seasonal Japanese served on fine tableware: chilled chawanmushi with eggplant in summer, sashimi such as bluefin tuna, and in autumn a sanma rice one diner called amazing. One regular never looks at the menu and simply leaves it to the chef; à la carte works too. The sake list is wide, with rarities like a sparkling sake from Okayama, and the value draws praise. Despite the location it feels calm, not touristy, and the counter invites chat with the chef and neighbors. Lunch on Wednesday and Friday to Sunday is an omakase (¥5,800, two or more, book by the day before). Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Counter kappo run by the owner alone (September 2025 review; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The owner was managing everything alone, but the dishes were presented efficiently, one by one. The tableware was also quite exquisite. The selection of drinks was extensive, and I even got to try a rare sparkling Japanese sake from Okayama." — September 2025, lunch course.
"I usually don't even look at the menu and just let the master prepare dishes for me. It's a hidden gem for creative Japanese cuisine in Minami." — December 2025.

It usually opens at 18:00; a 17:00 start and weekend lunch need a reservation by the day before. Look for the green lantern. Cards and e-money accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_shoan_dotonbori.notes: [Japanese · grill-your-own dried fish over charcoal off Dotonbori] A basement izakaya under a green lantern in Dotonbori 2-chome, open since 2002, where you grill Shizuoka dried fish and vegetables yourself over a tabletop charcoal brazier. The assorted platter brings mackerel, horse mackerel and shishamo; shiitake come out bursting with juice, and there's a surprisingly good beef platter of thick tongue, wagyu short rib and tenderloin. Summer adds hamo with grated daikon and ponzu. Order the kamameshi when you sit down, since it's cooked to order and takes over 30 minutes; the salmon and ikura is the pick. Ingredients are mostly domestic, and the sake and shochu lists are strong. The room is calm, with a counter and tatami tables. Book a day ahead for weekend lunch or a 17:00 start.

chef_bio.background: Charcoal-grill izakaya (Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.philosophy: Safe ingredients, mainly from domestic producers (Tabelog listing).

"This restaurant is known for its delicious kamameshi (rice cooked in an iron pot), with the salmon and ikura (salmon roe) version being exceptional! It takes over 30 minutes to prepare, so be sure to order it right away." — November 2025.

osaka_egami_teppan_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a hidden teppan izakaya open until 3 am in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A teppan izakaya at the very end of a narrow corridor in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, running for about 27 years, whose sliding door opens onto a cozy counter and a cheerful owner. The Chinese-style fried rice comes from a recipe shared by Nakamura, a friend of the owner's mother. One regular has lost count of visits; the draw is drinking food from the griddle: kasu hari (abura kasu with crisp mizuna, ¥770), ten cheese, sautéed scallops, and okonomiyaki such as pork and egg crowned with a runny fried egg. Finish with salt yakisoba with crisp pork fat, or a curry yakisoba. It's often full of reservations, so book or call ahead. Open until 03:00; closed Sundays; cash only; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Teppan izakaya (official site on toxnavi.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained). The Chinese-style fried rice comes from a recipe shared by Nakamura, a friend of the owner's mother (May 2026 review).

"Okonomiyaki with Pork and Egg → It came topped with a fried egg. At first, the combination of the runny egg and the soft okonomiyaki made it easy to eat." — December 2025.

osaka_menya_odashi_to_niku_to_uchihonmac.notes: [Ramen · chicken paitan and clam shoyu, with wagyu sushi, by Tanimachi 4-chome] A lunch-only shop on the ground floor of the Dia Palace building in Uchihonmachi (the clam-and-chicken ramen shop Choro is upstairs), open since November 2024. Every regular bowl is ¥900. The paitan, the shop says, is a "triple soup" of three chickens, Yamagata pork and Kuroge wagyu tendon; one diner smelled a neighbor's bowl and called the aroma "comparable to tonkotsu ramen." For something lighter, the chicken and clam shoyu comes with thin noodles and yuzu. Add the ¥400 wagyu roast sushi, seared in front of you, or the ¥300 seared chashu-mayo rice bowl. A soy-milk cold tantanmen with yodare-dori chicken ran in summer 2026 and drew raves, though one diner found it bland. Lunch only, closed Sunday and Monday, cash only; one diner found it closed before last order.

osaka_menya_kunimaru_utsubo_koen_mae.notes: [Ramen · miso ramen specialist facing Utsubo Park] A branch of a miso-only ramen chain in front of Utsubo Park, open since 2021 with plenty of tables. The base is the chain's Hokkaido 100-year miso, a salty aged red miso it sears to draw out depth; one diner found it rich and robust, "perfect for when you're craving a rich bowl." If that's too strong for you, the silver miso uses a milder Kyushu barley miso, though one diner found it too mild. The gold miso is seared with white wine, almond and sansho; a spicy miso (¥980) comes in three heats. Lunch sets run about ¥900 with fried rice or plain rice, though one diner found the set ramen too simple and another warned off the fried rice. There's a kids' miso ramen too. Lunch can draw a short line.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the miso-ramen-only chain Menya Kunimaru (official site kunimaru.net).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Miso is a health food": four base misos, seared to draw out richness and aroma; medium-thick egg noodles and whole-wheat noodles (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The broth has a rich and robust flavor, showcasing the depth and umami of the miso… Despite its strong seasoning, the ramen is well-balanced." — October 2026, Hokkaido 100-year miso ramen.
"It has a mild miso flavor, and if you're looking for a rich and deep miso ramen… I recommend the 100-Year Miso Ramen instead." — June 2026, silver miso ramen.

osaka_men_dobu_uchihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · chicken paitan and big chashu set meals in Uchihonmachi] A small counter of about 10 seats a few minutes from Sakaisuji-Honmachi, running since 2011 and specializing in chicken paitan. The ajitama paitan (¥1,000) is rich yet relatively light, with thick-cut pork-belly chashu; at lunch you get a free large serving of noodles or rice. The other draw is the chashu set meal: 150 g or 250 g of chashu with mayonnaise and black pepper, a neatly rounded mound of rice, kimchi and soup, ¥1,300 for the large. There are also a classic ramen one diner found nostalgic, and Taiwanese mazesoba. Buy tickets at the machine outside; it takes ¥1,000 notes only. Snug, so not for groups. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

"I chose the 150g option, which came with plenty of flavorful chashu, mayonnaise, kimchi, and soup… The rice was beautifully shaped into a perfect round mound." — August 2026.

osaka_menya_yama_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · clear, slightly sweet shoyu until 6 am Fri–Sat in Honmachi] A busy office-district ramen shop near Sakaisuji-Honmachi with good turnover at lunch and late hours: until 23:00 most nights and 06:00 into Saturday and Sunday. The signature shoyu ramen (¥950) is a clear, gentle broth with a hint of sweetness in the soy, with chashu, menma, red onion and chili; flat noodles are ¥100 more, and the garlic comes on the side; one diner found it changed the bowl a lot. You choose noodle firmness and add-ons like yuzu peel and onion. The "umakara" (¥990) adds a stronger chili kick to that sweet shoyu. There's also a seafood shoyu, a tantanmen one diner came back for four times (chilled in summer), and a miso ramen. Free rice at lunch.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was indeed clear and gentle, with a hint of sweetness in the shoyu flavor… I added a bit of garlic, but it significantly changed the taste, so I prefer it without. I'm glad it was served separately." — August 2026, shoyu ramen ¥950.
"The spiciness from the chili was stronger than I expected. The base broth seems to use a slightly sweet soy sauce." — September 2026, umakara ramen ¥990.

osaka_menya_muchu_uchihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · light Hakata tonkotsu for ¥700 in the Dia Palace basement] A small, one-person ramen shop in the basement of the Dia Palace building in Uchihonmachi, the same building as Choro and Menya Odashi to Niku to, open since 2021. The tonkotsu ramen (¥700) is a milky but light, creamy pork-bone soup with very little odor, on straight thin Kyushu-style noodles cooked to the firmness you ask for. Everything else is a variation on that base: tonkotsu shoyu, sliced-garlic, butter, spicy, a tomato ramen and tantanmen. At lunch, ¥800 gets any regular ramen with mentaiko rice, diced chashu rice or plain rice, though the rice sometimes runs out. One diner found the staff attentive in explaining things to overseas visitors. It's light rather than heavy, so one diner wished it were more filling. Cards and QR accepted.

osaka_rantan_ramen_kawaramachi.notes: [Ramen · salty shoyu and shio, vegetable noodles and tantanmen at lunch in Honmachi] A bright, clean lunch-only counter of about 15 wall-facing seats under Chinese-style lanterns, a little inside its building near Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2019. The ramen runs salty: the shoyu is a seafood-and-pork broth "for those who enjoy bold flavors" with thick grilled chashu, and the shio hits hard with salt and pepper, which one diner likened to a much-upgraded Sugakiya. Beyond those there are vegetable noodles (¥950 large) with crab sticks and wood ear, a mild tantanmen (¥900) for the heat-shy, and sour-spicy noodles (¥900) topped with fresh tomato. Buy the ticket at the machine outside; water is self-service. Lunch is quieter by about 12:30. Cash only.

osaka_menya_shu_uehommachi.notes: [Ramen · thick chicken paitan from a one-chef counter by Uehommachi] A clean, eight-seat counter a few minutes from Uehommachi where one chef cooks fast, open since 2020. The chicken paitan (¥850) is thick and velvety, "rich yet not overwhelming" to one diner, with smooth straight thin noodles, tender chashu, long menma, red onion and bonito flakes. Stir in the spicy miso on the side little by little; it's hot. For more, there's an even richer, thicker paitan; a chuka soba one diner prefers; and a warm mazesoba. In summer, a chilled sea bream shio ramen with yuzu salt sells in limited numbers. Finish the soup with ¥100 rice. Mark your order on the sheet at the counter and pay cash after. One diner hit clumps of salt. Lunch only on Wednesday and Saturday.

osaka_mirai_ken_kawaramachi.notes: [Ramen · tantanmen in several flavors near Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A tantanmen shop behind a neon sign, opened in October 2025, that one diner learned is a sister shop of the Honmachi Chinese restaurant Koyouju. Start with the "Moto-Aji" original (¥950): a rich, only mildly spicy soup under a generous minced-meat sauce, bean sprouts and greens, on fairly thin noodles; one diner couldn't stop drinking the soup, which changes as the meat sauce mixes in. There are also "Shin-Aji" and miso versions, a shoyu tanmen and a sour-spicy suanshu tanmen; in summer a chilled spicy tantanmen (¥1,200) ran, though one diner wanted more heat. It also works as a casual Chinese spot: one diner had mapo tofu, pork and bean-sprout stir-fry, a half tantanmen and two lemon sours at 8 pm for under ¥2,500. Counter, tables and a terrace. Cards and QR accepted.

osaka_sushi_akazu_namba_premium.notes: [Sushi · red-vinegar sushi omakase at an eight-seat counter with a Namba night view] An eighth-floor, eight-seat counter of single-board hinoki in Soemoncho, open since February 2025, a sister shop of Sushi Akazu in Shinsaibashi. The omakase (¥19,800 in September 2026) runs in two seatings and builds around firm rice seasoned with aged red vinegar; one diner who worried it wouldn't suit loved it. Expect Hokkaido oysters in ponzu, a tuna trio of otoro, chutoro and marinated akami, steamed abalone whose liver sauce you finish over a little rice, sea urchin crowned with caviar, soft simmered anago, then a smoked-daikon toro-taku hand roll and a pudding-like tamago that plays dessert. One diner mentions the friendly chef, others the Minami night view, and two call it an anniversary or date place. BYO costs ¥5,000 a bottle.

osaka_jukusei_sushi_rita_namba.notes: [Sushi · aged-fish sushi omakase by Dotonbori] A reservation-only sushi counter on the third floor of a new building in Nishi-Shinsaibashi, open since May 2025, built around fish aged for different lengths of time. The ¥14,800 omakase runs to about 18 dishes: sea bream under a Tosa-vinegar jelly finished over binchotan, aori squid flash-frozen and finely scored, seven-day shima aji, dry-aged chutoro on rice kept warmer at 42°C so the fat melts, Densuke anago swished as shabu-shabu, and the signature botan ebi topped with shrimp roe and sea urchin. A fish-bone soup simmered for hours and a vanilla pudding close it. Diners praise the explanations and playful touches; one was surprised with a birthday plate. One diner noticed many overseas guests. There's a 5% service charge. Lunch on weekends.

chef_bio.background: Reservation-only aged-sushi counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Ultimate umami with time as an ally": different aging days for each fish and rice temperature varied by topping (October 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The medium fatty tuna, aged for 14 days, was served with rice at 42 degrees Celsius, the perfect temperature for melting the tuna's fat… The signature dish, botan ebi (sweet shrimp), was topped with uni (sea urchin) and egg." — October 2026, aged sushi omakase ¥14,800.
"A rich soup made by roasting fish bones for about 20 minutes and simmering for 4 hours." — October 2026.

osaka_agu_buta_shabu_butaya_aoi.notes: [Shabu-shabu · Okinawan Agu pork shabu-shabu in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A clean, reservation-only shabu-shabu room near Shinsaibashi that serves Okinawa's Agu pork, sliced and arranged like a rose; repeat diners come back for meat that is sweet and "not greasy at all." The ¥5,280 course opens with crunchy mozuku vinegar, then the hot pot, with homemade ponzu heaped with green onion, a sesame sauce and yuzu-kosho; wrap the pork around green onion or pickled island garlic. Staff explain the pot and serve the first round. Finish with zosui or Okinawa soba made with Ishigaki noodles, and add the sweet purple sweet potato tempura. One repeat diner always buys the ponzu to take home. Order a course or the hot pot per person, or a per-head charge applies. There's a second branch in Namba.

osaka_horumon_gibier_myojo_sennichimae.notes: [Standing bar · horumon and game, from kangaroo to badger, by Nippombashi] A retro standing bar behind a plastic-sheet door just off Sennichimae-dori, picked for Tabelog's tachinomi 100 in 2025, where 1980s and 90s J-pop plays on a big screen and you mix your own highball from bottled soda. The owner runs the shop with two female staff members. The draw is fresh offal and game: Matsusaka beef garlic small intestine (¥580), a seared Miyazaki beef yukhoe with egg yolk (¥980), and a kangaroo tenderloin steak (¥720) diners find tender, juicy and not gamey. Venison and wild boar are staples; pheasant, badger (as a winter hot pot), camel and sea lion turn up when in stock, camel announced on the shop's Instagram. Liver and the rarer cuts go fast, so come at opening; there can be a line. The weekend curry wins praise from the few who order it. Portions are small and prices exclude tax. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Standing bar for horumon and game; Tabelog tachinomi 100, 2025 (Tabelog). The owner runs the shop with two female staff members (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Horumon of Matsusaka and Miyazaki beef; game meats.

anecdotes.text: "The meat was more tender than I had imagined, with no strong odor or gamey taste, juicy and light… quite similar to the lean meat of Wagyu." — October 2026, kangaroo tenderloin ¥720.
"Today, I tried badger, kangaroo, and wild boar, and the badger was amazing! However, it seems that grilling it has a strong smell, so it was prepared in a hot pot instead." — September 2026.

osaka_mayonaka_kitchen_usagi.notes: [Late-night diner · omurice and izakaya snacks from midnight to 8 am in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A ten-seat U-shaped counter with no big sign, behind a curtain and sliding door in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, that keeps reverse hours: midnight to 8 am, Tuesday to Sunday. The owner calls it a casual izakaya, so order a drink, but the dish to get is the omurice (¥780), the most popular to one diner: fragrant ketchup rice under rich egg with a tangy, thick ketchup. The macaroni salad with a hint of curry, octopus-shaped red sausages and pork kimchi go with a lemon chuhai; there's also marinated mackerel and octopus sashimi. One diner found it packed at 5:30 am; another has come for over 10 years. Spend runs about ¥1,400. Cash only.

osaka_noodle_cafe_q_mydome.notes: [Ramen · cafe-style ramen with coffee on the ground floor of My Dome Osaka] A big, calm, 100-seat ramen cafe on the ground floor of the My Dome Osaka exhibition hall, opened in August 2025 by the company behind Choro. The bowls are light: a chicken-based shoyu on straight thin noodles with thin slices of duck chashu, a niboshi shoyu (¥950) and a miso, with seasonal changes. The popular lunch set pairs shoyu ramen with yakimeshi and a drip coffee for ¥1,000; others come with lu rou fan or seasoned rice, and there's a kara-age set (¥900) and Basque cheesecake. Two diners found the shoyu on the salty side. With Wi-Fi, outlets, raised tatami seating and a kids' menu, it suits families and laptop lunches. Order at the touch-panel ticket machine and clear your own table.

osaka_menya_kei_yariyamachi.notes: [Ramen · chicken-tonkotsu paitan, tsukemen and abura soba by Tanimachi 4-chome] A small counter of about seven seats near Tanimachi 4-chome, with tables upstairs when it fills after noon, running since 2018. The ramen (¥900) is a chicken and pork-bone paitan that one diner found hearty, with short medium-thin noodles and thin, well-seasoned pork-belly chashu; add the A set (+¥150) for two kara-age and rice. The tsukemen (¥980) pairs medium-thick chewy noodles with a chicken, pork-bone and seafood dip, light in body but oily on top, with a little acidity. The abura soba (¥890) comes regular or Japanese-style, dressed in soy and shrimp oil over thick glossy noodles; at lunch ¥1,070 adds kara-age and rice. One diner found the menma flat and the welcome cool. Dinner on weekends depends on the soup.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2022–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The soup is a chicken and pork bone white broth, and after taking a sip, I could taste the richness of the chicken combined with the depth and umami of the pork bone… The noodles are short, medium-thin, with a nice chewiness." — September 2025, ramen ¥900.
"The dipping sauce was made from chicken, pork bones, and seafood. It had a light consistency with a generous amount of oil on the surface… a hint of acidity." — September 2025, tsukemen ¥980.

osaka_menya_ino_naka_no_kawazu.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; shoyu ramen.
osaka_menya_ino_naka_no_kawazu.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken broth; rare chashu.
osaka_menya_ino_naka_no_kawazu.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–14:00 (L.O. 13:30) until the soup sells out; closing days vary (Tabelog). 2026 reviews describe it as an Italian restaurant at night with ramen at lunch, one specifying weekday lunch. Line after 12:00 (April 2026). Circle your order on a sheet. Cards and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_menya_ino_naka_no_kawazu.notes: [Ramen · herb-scented shio ramen at lunch in an Italian restaurant, Awajimachi] A stylish room between Honmachi and Yodoyabashi that serves Italian food at night and turns into a ramen shop at lunch, open since March 2025. The shio ramen (¥1,000) is the bowl to get: a rich chicken and aromatic-vegetable broth drawn out with herbs and spices, which one diner likened to Italian dressing, with rare chashu and thin noodles. A lemon wedge comes on the side; squeeze it in midway for a brighter, almost pho-like finish. Add umeboshi or yuzu-kosho for more changes. One diner brought a 2026 Kansai ramen guide that gave the shio a semi-grand prize. There's also a shoyu, and a chashu rice bowl that sells out. A small noodle portion is very small. Lunch only; a line formed after noon one April day.

chef_bio.background: Ramen at lunch in a restaurant that serves Italian at night (2026 reviews; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Shio broth drawn with herbs and spices, per a 2026 Kansai ramen guide cited by a diner (June 2026).

anecdotes.text: "The broth, infused with the aroma and flavor of herbs typical of Italian cuisine, was rich and savory… a lemon for flavor enhancement is provided by default, and squeezing it… gives a slightly Asian twist, reminiscent of pho broth." — May 2026, shio ramen.
"I added umeboshi (pickled plum), yuzu pepper, and menma (bamboo shoots) as toppings. I really liked the thin, smooth noodles that paired well with the broth." — June 2026.

osaka_doro_soba_masa_sakaisuji_honmachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; fried toppings; kara-age bowl.
osaka_doro_soba_masa_sakaisuji_honmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken and vegetable "doro" soup; chashu.
osaka_doro_soba_masa_sakaisuji_honmachi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30–22:45); Sun 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–23:00; closing days vary; closed 1 January (Tabelog). Ticket machine; staff help if unsure (August 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_doro_soba_masa_sakaisuji_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · thick chicken-and-vegetable "doro" soba near Kitahama] A small office-district counter between Kitahama and Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2020 and, one diner says, one of the chain's last two shops along with Nara, serving doro soba: a soup of chicken and vegetables simmered until they dissolve, so thick it clings to the noodles "like a purée." Two diners were surprised how easy it is to drink and how clean the finish is; one found the flavor ordinary beneath the texture. Choose your richness, from the basic bowl up to the extra-thick Oni Kyoku (¥1,600), or a spicy version (¥1,500). Toppings of fried green onion and eringi add aroma, and pink pickled ginger from the counter sweetens and shifts the soup. At lunch there's a doro soba set with a mini chashu rice bowl, or add a mini kara-age bowl for ¥100. Buy a ticket first; staff help if you're unsure. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Branch of a small doro-soba chain; one diner counts this shop and one in Nara as the remaining branches (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The soup was a thick, creamy broth, reminiscent of a purée, made by simmering chicken and vegetables until they lost their shape… despite the richness of the soup, the aftertaste was surprisingly refreshing." — August 2026, lunch doro soba, richness level 2.
"Adding ginger brings a subtle sweetness to the broth, completely transforming its rich flavor." — August 2026.

osaka_ramen_kasumi_awaza.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; soy-based tare and mazesoba sauce.
osaka_ramen_kasumi_awaza.vegan_detail: Not vegan: niboshi broth with back fat; chashu; egg.
osaka_ramen_kasumi_awaza.hours_raw: Mon–Wed and public holidays 11:00–15:00 and 18:00–23:00; Thu 08:00–15:00 and 18:00–22:00; Fri 08:00–15:00 and 18:00–23:00; Sat 09:00–15:00 and 18:00–23:00; Sun 09:00–23:00 straight through; open year-round (Tabelog). Ticket machine inside; chairs for the line outside; self-service water; paper aprons (September 2026). Cards, IC cards, e-money and QR incl. Alipay and WeChat Pay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_ramen_kasumi_awaza.notes: [Ramen · niboshi chuka soba with back fat, on Tabelog's Ramen 100 since 2017, in Kyomachibori] A seven-seat counter near Awaza, open since 2012 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2017 to 2025, with early-morning hours from Thursday to Sunday and late nights most days. The niboshi ramen (¥950) is gentler than the name suggests: a mild soy base with floating back fat and a pleasant niboshi bitterness, on medium-thick curly noodles; one diner thought of Yamagata ramen. The special niboshi mazesoba (¥1,300) is the other draw: sweet-savory soy and concentrated niboshi over wide, chewy curly noodles from Kyoto's Menya Teigaku, piled with block and rare chashu; one diner said the regular version would do. There can be a line at night, with chairs outside. Cards, e-money and QR accepted. A second shop is in Nakazakicho.

chef_bio.background: Niboshi ramen shop; main branch, with a second shop in Nakazakicho (October 2026 review). Tabelog Ramen 100 (WEST 2017–2022, OSAKA 2023–2025).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was a mild soy sauce base, leaving a pleasant niboshi bitterness in the aftertaste… The presence of back fat and curly noodles gave me the impression that it might be reminiscent of Yamagata-style ramen." — October 2026, niboshi ramen ¥950.

"The noodles are wide, flat noodles from the long-established noodle shop 'Menya Teigaku' in Kyoto. With a slight curl, they hold the sauce well, offering a chewy texture and a firm bite." — October 2026, special niboshi mazesoba ¥1,300.

osaka_ibukuro_washizukami_shitennoji.vegan_detail: Not vegan: niboshi; back fat; beef tendon and clams in the shio; karasumi; egg sauce.
osaka_ibukuro_washizukami_shitennoji.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:30 (L.O. 15:00) and 18:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:30); hours may change (Tabelog). Order by number and pay first, cash on the counter (October 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Waits of about 10 minutes at noon (October 2026).
osaka_ibukuro_washizukami_shitennoji.notes: [Ramen · shoyu on medium-thick curly noodles and karasumi mazesoba, by Shitennoji] A tiny eight-seat shop near Shitennoji, open since 2022 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 in 2024 and 2025. The noodles are the point: robust, flat, medium-thick and curly, which one diner was "a bit moved" to find. The shoyu ramen is light with niboshi umami (¥1,250 with wontons and egg); the rich shoyu adds a strong garlic hit, aosa seaweed and fish powder to stir in. For heat, the Inazuma chuka soba and mazesoba layer chili, sansho and black pepper over sweet soy and back fat. A repeat diner's favorite is the chilled mazesoba with karasumi, green onion and niboshi, finished with a warm egg sauce, though the shio with beef tendon, clams and niboshi may top it. Seats are few, so expect a short wait at noon. Pay first, cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop; Tabelog Ramen OSAKA 100, 2024 and 2025 (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Shoyu ramen on medium-thick curly noodles; mazesoba.

anecdotes.text: "It was light yet flavorful, with a nice umami from the niboshi (dried sardines). Then came the medium-thick curly noodles. I was a bit moved to encounter such a perfect noodle." — October 2026, shoyu ramen with wontons and egg ¥1,250.

"With a combination of chili peppers, sansho pepper, and black pepper, the spices amplify the flavors, while the sweetness of the soy sauce and back fat accelerates the stimulation." — October 2026, Inazuma chuka soba.

osaka_shinka_bakushin_kyomachibori.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork-bone broth (with seafood, one diner thought); chashu.
osaka_shinka_bakushin_kyomachibori.hours_raw: Mon–Thu 11:00–16:00 and 18:00–24:00; Fri–Sun 11:00–14:30; hours may change (Tabelog). Free self-serve rice with pickles, tsukudani and takana at lunch; rice can sell out (2026 reviews). Cards incl. UnionPay, IC cards, iD, QUICPay and QR incl. WeChat Pay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_shinka_bakushin_kyomachibori.notes: [Ramen · rich tonkotsu with free rice at lunch near Higobashi] A second-floor ramen shop near Higobashi with flashy decor, open since 2012 and the main branch of its name. The tonkotsu ramen (¥950) is a rich, slightly grainy pork-bone soup with a pleasant pork aroma, deep but not too salty, on thick, firm noodles; one diner tasted seafood in it too. Two chashu come with it: a smoky, sweet-fatted belly block and a meaty loin. At lunch the rice is free and self-serve, with pickled greens, tsukudani and takana; one diner had two bowls, and when it sold out the staff found some leftovers. Add garlic and chili powder from the table. The black tonkotsu seemed the more popular order to one diner. Open until midnight Monday to Thursday, lunch only Friday to Sunday.

chef_bio.background: Tonkotsu ramen shop, main branch (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I could definitely taste the strong flavor of pork bone. However, while it has depth, it's not overly salty, with a strong umami and a grainy texture from the fat… The noodles are thick and have a firm bite." — September 2026, tonkotsu ramen ¥950.
"There were two types of chashu: the belly block was tender and had a pleasant sweetness from the fat, while the loin was packed with robust meat flavor." — September 2026.

osaka_okamoto_shoten_kitahama.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken paitan; seafood broth; chashu; egg.
osaka_okamoto_shoten_kitahama.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:00–14:30; closed Sun; hours may change (Tabelog). Free mini rice bowl if you arrive by 11:30; almond tofu or black coffee after 13:30 (September–October 2026). Full by 11:15 one September day. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_okamoto_shoten_kitahama.notes: [Ramen · thick chicken paitan and full toppings at lunch in Kitahama] A bright basement ramen shop in the Kitahama office district, open since 2020 for lunch Monday to Saturday; one September day it was full by 11:15. Arrive by 11:30 for a free mini rice bowl. The chicken nikomi ramen (¥900) is a thick, creamy chicken paitan with a sweet chicken-fat finish that doesn't feel heavy afterward; pick thin or medium-thick noodles. The chicken and seafood (¥900) is flavorful but not too heavy. For +¥300 the full toppings bury the noodles in grilled and rare chashu, egg, nori and green onion. Tsukemen and a chicken shoyu round out the menu. After 13:30 you get almond tofu or a black coffee on the house. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Chicken ramen shop, Kitahama branch (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a rich chicken paitan, simmered to perfection. It has a thick, creamy texture that concentrates the umami of the chicken, with a lingering sweetness from the fat." — September 2026, chicken nikomi ramen ¥900.
"I arrived around 11:15, but it was already full… I was informed that a mini rice bowl would come with it until 11:30." — September 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 岡本商店 北浜店、大阪市中央区平野町2-3-12、北浜から425m、月〜土 11:00〜14:30、日休み、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、15席(カウンター7、テーブル8)、2020年4月6日開店。口コミ(2024年10月〜2026年10月): 11時過ぎに4人待ち、11時半までに来るとミニ丼が無料、ラーメンとチャーシュー丼、地下の目立たない場所、つけ麺大300g 1,000円(2024年)、ねぎ増し無料(2024年)、11時15分で満席、鶏煮込みラーメン900円、鶏脂の甘み、細麺か中太麺、炙りかレアのチャーシュー、味玉、硬めのメンマ、食後に重くない、鶏醤油、鶏魚介、つけ麺、醤油ラーメンと唐揚げ丼、清潔、親切なスタッフ、濃厚な鶏白湯、全部のせ+300円で2種のチャーシュー・味玉・海苔・ねぎ、期間限定の杏仁豆腐、13時半以降は杏仁豆腐かブラックコーヒーのサービス、鶏魚介ラーメン900円は重すぎない。

osaka_gyokusei_ya_sennichimae.vegan_detail: Ask. Red-bean and kinako ohagi contain no obvious animal products, but no source lists the ingredients.
osaka_gyokusei_ya_sennichimae.hours_raw: From 14:00 until sold out; closed Wed, Thu, Sun and public holidays, open during the equinox and Obon weeks (Tabelog). No fixed closing time; one diner joined the line at 16:00 and waited two hours (October 2026). Lines of about 40 by opening and waits of 1¾–2 hours (October 2026). Takeaway only. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_gyokusei_ya_sennichimae.notes: [Sweets · made-to-order ohagi with a two-hour line, by Nippombashi] A small, long-standing ohagi shop off Sennichimae-dori (often called Tamaseiya), picked for Tabelog's sweets lists from 2017 to 2026, that opens at 14:00 four days a week and closes when it sells out. There's one thing to buy: a box of six small ohagi (¥1,170), choosing up to two of smooth red bean, chunky red bean and kinako, made fresh after you order, so the line is slow; October diners waited one and three-quarter to two hours, and about 40 people were queued by opening. The anko is gently sweet with a touch of salt, the kinako fine, the rice soft and lightly crushed, and even people who dislike ohagi like them. Eat the kinako ones the same day; anko keeps until the next morning. Takeaway only, cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ohagi shop; Tabelog sweets 100 (2017–2022) and Japanese sweets WEST 100 (2023, 2026) (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "I arrived at 1:20 PM, 40 minutes before opening, and there were already about 20 people in line… by opening time, around 40 people were waiting." — October 2026.

"The soybean flour is pleasantly sweet, and the red bean paste has a gentle sweetness with a hint of salt. The soft texture… combined with the chewy, slightly crushed glutinous rice is simply delightful!" — October 2026.

osaka_pieno_vivace_namba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: pasta and pizza are the core; baguette with the ajillo; spring-roll wrappers.
osaka_pieno_vivace_namba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: uni cream pasta, carpaccio, prosciutto, burrata, beef.
osaka_pieno_vivace_namba.hours_raw: Wed–Mon 17:00–24:00 (L.O. 23:00); closed Tue (Tabelog). Small: reserve for Friday and Saturday evenings and for tables; call for the counter with three or more (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_pieno_vivace_namba.notes: [Italian · uni pasta, carpaccio and wine in a tiny Ura-Namba bar] A small, nearly always full Italian bar at the end of a backstreet in Ura-Namba, open since 2009 and one of several PIENO shops. It shares the main shop's menu, so start with the three-fish carpaccio (¥1,298) and the fig, mascarpone and prosciutto spring rolls, add the oyster ajillo or a skirt steak, and finish with the signature uni cream pasta (¥1,188). Pasta comes firm; one diner came back ten years on for the unchanged Genovese. Handwritten specials change daily, the wine list explains itself, and the sangria is homemade. One diner spent about ¥5,000 with drinks, another about ¥8,000 with two bottles of red between two. It's cramped, so skip it with big luggage and reserve for Friday or Saturday evenings.

chef_bio.background: One of the PIENO Italian bars run by the Yasumaru group, which lists several PIENO shops in Namba and one in Kochi (official site yasumaru.co.jp).

anecdotes.text: "The basic menu is the same as the main Pieno location, but there are many handwritten daily specials. The signature dish at Pieno is the sea urchin pasta… The carpaccio here is a standout, made with fresh seafood." — August 2026.

"I particularly recommend the Genovese pasta. I used to come here just to eat this pasta ten years ago. I was really happy to see it still on the menu and that the taste remained the same." — October 2026.

osaka_wabisuke_namba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: dashi-soy seasoning throughout; kara-age, ham katsu, fried horse mackerel and tempura; spaghetti salad.
osaka_wabisuke_namba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi in the obanzai and omelet; beef, pork miso soup, seafood.
osaka_wabisuke_namba.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 11:30–15:00 (L.O. 14:30; lunch ends when sold out) and 17:30–23:30 (L.O. 23:00); Sun 17:30–23:30 (Tabelog). Lunch lines of 10–20 from before opening; staff take orders in the line (September–October 2026). Evenings are easier. PayPay accepted; no cards or e-money (Tabelog).
osaka_wabisuke_namba.notes: [Izakaya · obanzai counter with a ¥900 niku dashimaki lunch in Ura-Namba] A twelve-seat counter in the Ura-Namba backstreets, open since 2020, that is two places in one. At lunch the line forms before opening for the ¥900 set: pick one of six mains, most famously the niku dashimaki, a fluffy, freshly rolled dashi omelet topped with sweet-savory beef, with obanzai, a little sashimi, a big bowl of tonjiru and rice refills; or swap the rice for a draft beer. Staff take your order in the line. At night it's an easier, friendly izakaya: the "five" obanzai platter that one regular says usually comes with six, thick-cut ham katsu, chikuwa tempura with shibazuke tartare, the dashimaki again, and highballs. It's the main shop of its name. PayPay or cash.

chef_bio.background: Obanzai izakaya, main shop (Tabelog; 2020–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The meat dashimaki set meal is priced at JPY 900 and includes the main dish, four types of daily obanzai, pickles, and a hearty pork miso soup… The fluffy dashimaki, perfectly cooked without any burnt edges, pairs wonderfully with the richly flavored beef." — November 2025.
"As usual, the assorted obanzai came with 6 types instead of 5, which was a nice surprise!" — October 2026, a ninth visit.

osaka_tempura_shinsaibashi_ittetsu.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat-flour tempura batter is the meal; tentsuyu dipping sauce; curry finish option.
osaka_tempura_shinsaibashi_ittetsu.vegan_detail: Not vegan: shrimp, fish, wagyu and sea urchin in the course; ikura rice.
osaka_tempura_shinsaibashi_ittetsu.hours_raw: Wed–Thu 17:30–22:00 (food L.O. 20:30); Fri–Sun and public holidays 11:30–14:00 (food L.O. 13:00) and 17:30–22:00 (L.O. 20:30); closed Mon and Tue (next day if a holiday) (Tabelog). 10% service charge; same-day cancellation fee (Tabelog). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_tempura_shinsaibashi_ittetsu.notes: [Tempura · counter tempura courses with a shaved-ice finish in Shinsaibashi] A calm twelve-seat tempura counter on Shinsaibashi-suji, open since 2018, the second shop of Tempura Osakaya Kusatetsu in Fukushima. The chef, Shin Tamura, trained at the Nikko Hotel and has 32 years in Japanese cuisine. Courses begin with a look at the day's ingredients, then two shrimp, fried one piece at a time in front of you, with three salts and tentsuyu and a suggestion for each. In autumn there's matsutake as tempura or a dobin-mushi with scallop and ginkgo, and one diner called the Beni Haruka sweet potato the best tempura sweet potato ever eaten. Finish with tendon, curry or rice with ikura, then a fluffy shaved ice and dandelion coffee. Lunch on Friday to Sunday is the way in: courses from ¥7,700 with a drink, or ¥10,000; reviewers' spend ran up to ¥15,000–20,000. Explanations are thorough. 10% service charge.

chef_bio.background: Second shop of Tempura Osakaya Kusatetsu in Fukushima, Osaka (August and October 2026 reviews). The chef, Shin Tamura, trained at the Nikko Hotel and has 32 years in Japanese cuisine (Tabelog listing).
chef_bio.philosophy: Ingredients such as Nagasaki live shrimp, A5 wagyu fillet, Nemuro sea urchin and young ayu; house-treated water adjusted per ingredient; shaved ice from house ice frozen over two days (as listed by an October 2026 reviewer).

anecdotes.text: "First, they present the tempura options for the day… There are three types of salt and a dipping sauce available… The course began with two shrimp… The dessert was quite unique, featuring shaved ice and dandelion coffee." — September 2026, lunch course ¥7,700.

"I was offered a choice between tempura and dobin mushi for the matsutake mushroom… the sweet potato (today it was Beni Haruka) was the best tempura sweet potato I have ever had!" — October 2026, lunch.

osaka_tori_shin_higashi_shinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: tare on skewers; ponzu; fried gizzards and tulip wings; noodle finish.
osaka_tori_shin_higashi_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken in every course; chicken-bone mizutaki broth.
osaka_tori_shin_higashi_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and days before/after holidays 18:00–24:00, from 17:00 with a reservation; closed Sun and public holidays; may close early when ingredients run out (Tabelog). Seating limited to 2½ hours when busy; three-item otoshi ¥660 (Tabelog). Cards incl. UnionPay, QUICPay and QR accepted (Tabelog). Lively and loud (October 2026).
osaka_tori_shin_higashi_shinsaibashi.notes: [Yakitori · Hakata mizutaki and yakitori down a Higashi-Shinsaibashi alley] A busy chicken restaurant tucked down an alley in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, running since 2007 and often hard to book. The hot pot is the reason to come: a Hakata mizutaki whose rich, creamy collagen broth arrives as a solid block and melts in the pot, deep and gentle with tender chicken; finish with zosui or noodles, and reserve it ahead. Around it, there's a five-kind chicken sashimi plate with no off flavors, tataki, salt-grilled skewers, tsukune with egg yolk, fried gizzards and fried tulip wings the size of a KFC piece. Portions are big. Service is quick and the room loud enough that one diner couldn't hear the table. Seating is capped at 2½ hours when busy; ¥660 otoshi.

chef_bio.background: Yakitori and mizutaki restaurant (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The recommended hot pot features a broth rich in chicken flavor, delivering a deep and gentle taste from the very first bite… worth visiting primarily for the hot pot." — April 2026.
"The broth for the hot pot comes in a solid block! As it melts, it transforms into a rich and flavorful broth. I also love the fried chicken gizzards here." — September 2025.

Opening times not listed. Choose noodles (150 g or 200 g, same price), vegetables, back fat and garlic. Stamp card; free self-serve kimchi (2026 reviews). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_menya_gaten_no_ran_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style MAZE soba and Taiwanese mazesoba in the Yodoyabashi office district] A twelve-seat office-district shop between Yodoyabashi and Kitahama, open since 2015 and open daily. The MAZE soba is the order: flat, thick, chewy noodles in a rich soy dressing, under vegetables, back fat, garlic and a punch of black pepper, all adjustable from less to extra, with 200 g of noodles for the price of 150 g. The Taiwanese mazesoba (¥1,050) has its own repeat diner, and the creamy chicken paitan (¥1,000) is the lighter way in. Self-serve kimchi is free, and a stamp card leads to a gold card with free rice. One diner asked for extra fat and got extra garlic. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Mazesoba and ramen shop, Honmachi-Yodoyabashi branch (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The rich soy sauce dressing paired perfectly with the hearty flat thick noodles… You can choose between 150g and 200g of noodles, and customize the amount of vegetables, fat, and garlic from less to extra." — March 2025, MAZE soba.
"The chicken paitan ramen costs JPY 1000, and the chashu (braised pork) is tender and delicious." — October 2026, ninth visit.

osaka_mendokoro_amakawa_kujo.notes: [Ramen · Agu pork and Tanba black chicken shoyu and shio, with inventive limited bowls, by Kujo] A nine-seat counter near Kujo, open since 2019 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen 100 in 2024 and 2025, with lines at the 11:00 opening. A husband-and-wife team runs it; the owner trained at ramen shops before opening. The base is an additive-free double soup of Agu pork and Tanba black chicken with a layered fish dashi; the ajitama shoyu (¥1,250) floats Agu back fat over flat noodles from Tsurumi Seimen, with juicy Agu belly chashu. The shio is clear and mellow, its umami building as you go. For the simplest taste of broth and noodle, there's a kake-style shio or shoyu soba with only onion. Repeat diners come for the limited bowls: a stir-fried chicken-shoulder noodle tossed in a cast-iron pan, an Onomichi-style back-fat shoyu, chilled ramen in summer. Add the seasonal takikomi rice. Ticket machine, cash only; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter; Tabelog Ramen OSAKA 100, 2024 and 2025 (Tabelog). A husband-and-wife team runs it; the owner trained at ramen shops before opening (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: No chemical seasonings; Tanba black chicken delivered unfrozen; filtered water; domestic-wheat noodles from Tsurumi Seimen (2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.specialty: Agu pork shoyu; shio; limited bowls.

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a rich blend of Agu pork and Niwa black chicken, combined with both animal and seafood extracts. It starts off with a strong umami flavor from the meat, followed by a gentle aftertaste of dried fish." — October 2026, ajitama shoyu ramen ¥1,250.

"The domestic chicken shoulder meat and plenty of vegetables are stir-fried over high heat to achieve a fragrant finish… neither Mazesoba nor Yakisoba; it's a unique creation." — October 2026, limited stir-fried noodles ¥1,200.

osaka_miso_noodle_koji_hiranomachi.notes: [Ramen · rich miso on thick curly noodles near Kitahama] A fifteen-seat counter in the Kitahama office district, open since 2020 and run by the same people as the nearby Tsukemen Ide, with a lunch line that some diners call routine. The miso ramen (¥1,000) is rich and slightly gritty, with a pork-bone base beneath, on thick, chewy curly noodles of whole wheat, brightened by chopped purple onion and white negi with yuzu peel. Two variations stand out: the spicy miso, with five heat levels and the first three free, where the miso stays the star; and the "Wasan sansho" miso (¥1,100), whose aroma greets you at the door and gives a refreshing finish. Buy your ticket inside before you line up. Cards and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Miso ramen shop; sister of Tsukemen Ide (2021 and September 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is quite rich in miso flavor. You can taste the pork bone flavor beneath the miso, but there's a slight graininess… The noodles are thick, curly, and made from whole wheat, strong enough to stand up to the broth." — October 2026, miso ramen ¥1,000.
"The broth had a rich miso flavor without being heavy, and the fragrance and mild spiciness of the sansho created a refreshing aftertaste." — March 2026, Wasan sansho miso ramen ¥1,100.

osaka_tsukemen_ide_hiranomachi.notes: [Ramen · thick pork-bone and seafood tsukemen in Kitahama since 2011] A busy fifteen-seat tsukemen shop in the Kitahama office district, open since 2011, where lunch means buying a ticket, a short wait outside and often a shared table. The tsukemen (¥1,100) pairs glossy, chewy thick noodles with a strong wheat flavor and a thick, rich dipping soup of pork bone and seafood, "rich without being overly heavy," with chashu and menma already in it; one October diner got 300 g for ¥1,100. Finish with soup-wari from the table. Add all the toppings (¥600) or a rice bowl of shredded pork or niku-miso. There's also a curry tsukemen. One diner found it simply average. Its sister shop, Miso Noodle Koji, is a few blocks west. Cards and PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Tsukemen shop; sister of Miso Noodle Koji (Tabelog; 2021 and 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The glossy, chewy thick noodles are rich in wheat flavor… The dipping sauce, packed with the umami of pork bones and seafood, is thick and rich without being overly heavy." — October 2026.
"I ordered the Tsukemen (large) for JPY 1,100, which comes with 300g of noodles. The broth is rich and flavorful, with a strong seafood taste that clings well to the noodles." — October 2026.

osaka_tori_katori_i_ga_ika_taisho.notes: [Ramen · whipped chicken paitan by Taisho Station] A bright, clean seven-seat counter a block from Taisho Station, open since September 2024 and serving the chicken paitan that one diner hadn't found anywhere else in Taisho. The soup is whipped until frothy and creamy but not too heavy, on thin straight noodles, with two chashu: rare pork shoulder and a roasted or grilled pork belly. Choose shio, shoyu (the soy comes through strongly) or a spicy version; one diner found the extra noodles salty. Order rice (¥100) and you get takana and spicy mentaiko free, or go for the rare chashu bowl with egg yolk. In summer there are chilled bowls such as a sea bream and clam shio with tempura, which can sell out at lunch; one August evening there was a line of six. Closed Wednesdays; Tuesday is lunch only.

chef_bio.background: Chicken paitan ramen counter (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The whipped chicken paitan broth is truly delicious. The chashu comes in two varieties: rare pork shoulder chashu and chestnut pork roast." — January 2026, rich chicken paitan shio.

"The cold shio ramen featured medium-thick straight noodles topped with tempura, two slices of rare chashu, white onions, green onions, seaweed, and a citrus fruit, all in a light and delicious broth." — August 2026, chilled sea bream and clam shio ramen ¥1,300.

osaka_ramen_tokimaru_uehommachi.notes: [Ramen · bonito-kombu-pork shoyu with burdock, near Uehommachi] A seven-seat counter on Sennichimae-dori between Uehommachi and Tsuruhashi, open since 2016 with late hours after 19:00. The Tokimaru shoyu ramen (¥780) is a triple soup of bonito, kombu and pork bone with a gentle soy, on flat, medium-thick whole-wheat noodles, topped with cabbage, bean sprouts and the house signature: tender simmered burdock, which makes it taste distinctly Japanese. Add extra vegetables for a fuller bowl. The tsukemen (¥900 for 100 g) and a spicy tonkotsu shoyu draw mixed reviews, and one diner found the niboshi version too salty. In summer there's a sticky, spicy neba-neba chilled noodle with okra, yam and kimchi. Closes when the soup runs out.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; official site tokimaru.com).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles are flat, medium-thick, and made from whole wheat flour. The broth is a rich triple soup combining bonito, kombu kelp, and pork bones, seasoned with soy sauce… the standout ingredient is definitely the burdock root!" — October 2025, Tokimaru shoyu ramen ¥780.

"The rich pork bone broth was infused with seafood flavors, particularly strong notes of bonito… An unusual topping of burdock root was included, but it didn't leave a strong impression." — January 2026, tsukemen 100 g ¥900.

osaka_menya_seifuuken_awaza.notes: [Ramen · shrimp-bushi chuka men and shrimp abura soba by Awaza, with morning ramen] A clean, calm eight-seat shop two minutes from Awaza, opened in April 2026 and described by one diner as the next brand from Ramen Kasumi, with morning ramen from 8:00 on Friday to Sunday. Start with the Moto-Aji chuka men, a light but rich, slightly sweet shoyu on curly whole-wheat noodles, or go straight to the Shin-Aji ebi-bushi chuka men (¥1,000): a salt broth of house-made shrimp, squid and chicken bushi that blooms when you stir in the red shrimp oil, over chewy flat twisted noodles. The ebi shio abura soba is the other favorite. Use the table's niboshi vinegar and spicy mala takuan to change it up midway. Cash-only ticket machine; you may get a coupon for next time.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop described by an October 2026 diner as "Kasumi's next brand" (Ramen Kasumi); Tabelog.
chef_bio.philosophy: Menu board: "a fragrant oil soup made with homemade shrimp bushi, squid, and chicken bushi… Seifuuken's neo-Chinese ramen" (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Shrimp-bushi chuka men; ebi shio abura soba.

anecdotes.text: "When tasting the salt-based broth alone, it had a perfect saltiness and rich umami… Then I mixed in the red liquid that resembled shrimp oil… The flavor and aroma of shrimp spread throughout the broth." — September 2026, Shin-Aji ebi-bushi chuka men ¥1,000.

"The broth was light yet rich, offering a comforting and flavorful taste… The slightly sweet soy sauce flavor was well pronounced… The curly whole wheat noodles had a wonderful chewy and smooth texture." — September 2026, Moto-Aji chuka soba.

osaka_ramen_toride_kyomachibori.hours_raw: Daily 11:30–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); public holidays 11:30–22:00 (L.O. 21:45); closing days vary (Tabelog). Cards, IC cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog). LINE coupons.
osaka_ramen_toride_kyomachibori.notes: [Ramen · creamy clam paitan with dunk rice near Higobashi] A calm counter in Kyomachibori, open all day since 2017, whose Toride ramen is a milky clam paitan that one diner likened to clam chowder: thick and rich but with a clean, oceanic finish, on thin noodles with rare chashu and charred green onion. The owner is a woman, which surprised a reviewer expecting a samurai type from the name. Get the Toride set (¥1,100) and tip the "dunk rice" into the last of the soup for a risotto-like finish, or pair the bowl with a clam rice bowl and a well-seasoned egg. A chilled version comes with thicker chashu, and a gentle limited niboshi ramen has appeared. Light enough that one diner found it went down easily even with no appetite. Open daily until 23:00; cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Clam paitan ramen shop, Kyomachibori branch (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews). The owner is a woman, which surprised a reviewer expecting a samurai type from the name (April 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The Toride Ramen features a creamy and rich clam-based broth. It's thick yet has a refreshing aftertaste, perfectly complementing the thin noodles." — July 2026, Toride set.
"In a nutshell, it tastes like clam chowder, but it's impressive how it has been transformed into ramen… a delicious ramen that was light and easy to eat." — June 2025, clam paitan ramen.
