osaka_rakuraku_za_namba.notes: [Italian · one-person Italian bar with ¥890 iron-pan pasta lunches in Ura-Namba] A cozy, slightly chaotic Italian bar in the Ura-Namba backstreets behind the old Kabukiza, running since 1999 and cooked by one person. Weekday lunch is the find: ¥890–990 (2026) buys the day's pasta with a tangy mini salad and bread, or the Napolitan, served sizzling in an iron pan ringed with egg, in a large size one diner thought could feed three. The iron-pot doria hides a melting egg under ketchup rice and cheese, and the carbonara (¥890) pairs well with a ¥550 glass of white. Expect a wait: one diner waited about 20 minutes, and another saw a fellow diner carry plates to help. At night it's a wine bar with Italian plates (¥300 seat charge). On Friday to Sunday lunch the room becomes the curry shop Curry Ya Miyan. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Italian bar run by one person (September–October 2026 reviews); official site rakurakuza.smafo.biz.
chef_bio.philosophy: "Authentic Italian in a homey atmosphere, where you can eat and drink cheerfully" (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The iron pot was sizzling with a generous amount of ketchup-covered Neapolitan spaghetti! The edges of the pot were lined with eggs… a rich and nostalgic flavor!" — October 2026, iron-pot pasta lunch, large.
"Today's special pasta lunch for JPY 890. Includes a salad and toast. Since it's a one-man operation, it takes a little time." — September 2026.

osaka_anju_tei_soemoncho.notes: [Yakiniku · A5 wagyu and fresh horumon with a sauce for every cut, down a Soemoncho alley] A small yakiniku house hidden in an alley off Sennichimae-suji, open since 2022, with a five-seat counter below and private tatami rooms above, taking only three groups at a time. Non-offal cuts are A5 female Kuroge wagyu, the shop says, and the offal is chosen for freshness: start with the clean heart sashimi and the white senmai, then the seared yukhoe with egg yolk. Each cut comes with its own sauce, salt or dip, including a light Kyoto-style dip that washes away excess fat, and staff explain how to eat each one; the owner sears the wagyu yaki-shabu for you. Finish with the bright sudachi cold noodles. Diners spent ¥8,000–15,000. Open late; reserve for after 02:00. No small children.

chef_bio.background: Yakiniku restaurant (official site kyoto-anjutei.com; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Offal such as tongue, skirt, liver and mino chosen above all for freshness; other cuts limited to A5 female Kuroge wagyu; only three groups at a time (official site).

anecdotes.text: "Each type of meat is served with a different sauce… Especially the Kalbi, which I enjoyed with a Kyoto-style washing sauce, was refreshing with a nice umami and acidity." — September 2026.

"A5-rank Miyazaki beef strip loin, grilled by the owner. The beautifully marbled meat is quickly seared, igniting a flame. Enjoy it with refreshing ponzu sauce or rich, beautiful egg yolk." — October 2026, grilled wagyu shabu-shabu ¥2,800.

osaka_umi_nabe_tei_shinsaibashi.notes: [Hot pot · 1 kg oyster and shrimp hot pots in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A compact seafood hot-pot shop in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2023 and open until 1 am, built around two show-stoppers. The big oyster hot pot (about ¥2,500–2,700 per person) piles more than a kilo of plump oysters and big scallops into a rich miso-butter broth with pork and vegetables; finish with the miso-butter risotto or ramen, cheese optional. The shrimp shabu-shabu course brings about a kilo of shrimp to swish briefly, cook longer or eat raw, after five kinds of sashimi and two pieces of sushi, ending in shrimp-broth risotto and ice cream. Start with fresh Hiroshima oysters (3 for ¥990) or the three-shrimp tasting. Smoking is allowed. Cards accepted.

chef_bio.background: Seafood hot-pot restaurant, Shinsaibashi branch (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The popular 豪快牡蠣鍋 (Gokai Kaki Nabe) featured over 1 kg of carefully selected plump oysters and large scallops… The rich miso butter-based broth not only infused the oysters and scallops but also absorbed the flavors of pork and vegetables." — September 2026.

"The shrimp shabu-shabu came with about 1 kg (around 10 pieces), which was very satisfying. You can quickly dip them in the broth or leave them a bit longer for a firmer texture, and they can even be enjoyed raw." — August 2026, shrimp shabu-shabu course.

osaka_curry_ya_miyan_namba.hours_raw: Fri–Sun 11:30–15:00, until sold out (Tabelog). Runs in the Rakuraku Za space at weekend lunch (2026 reviews). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_curry_ya_miyan_namba.notes: [Curry · weekend-only three-curry plates in Ura-Namba] A Friday-to-Sunday lunch curry counter that takes over the Italian bar Rakuraku Za in the Ura-Namba backstreets. There's one order: the three-curry plate (¥1,300), which changes with the season but in every review has paired a beef and pork keema, a gentle vegetable potage curry and a pork green keema. Recent potages have been new potato, corn, scallop and seaweed; the keemas have run from spring cabbage to citrus and red miso. Each is mild and well balanced, and the menu suggests mixing all three at the end. Add grilled cheese (+¥100) or grilled corn (+¥200). Lovers of fiery curry may find it tame. It can sell out; one diner was charged less when a curry ran short. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Weekend curry shop run in the Rakuraku Za space (2026 reviews; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The potage had a gentle flavor, combining the sweetness and umami of the fresh vegetables with a hint of spice. The two types of keema were not overly spicy, offering a well-balanced spice profile." — March 2026, three types ¥1,300.
"The standout was definitely the scallop potage. What a creative idea! The Beef, Pork, Shrimp, and Tomato Keema was also exceptional." — April 2026.

osaka_sosaku_washoku_jampa.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seafood, wagyu and dashi throughout the omakase.
osaka_sosaku_washoku_jampa.hours_raw: Mon–Sat and public holidays 17:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); closed Sun; seating may be limited to about 2½ hours (Tabelog). À la carte from 20:00 (November 2025). Courses ¥8,800 and ¥11,000; all-you-can-drink ¥5,000 (2026 reviews). Hard to find: call when close (Tabelog; April 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners) and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_sosaku_washoku_jampa.notes: [Japanese · hidden creative washoku omakase on a 7th floor in Amemura] A hideaway on the seventh floor of an Amemura building across from BIG STEP, reached through a narrow alley on the building's south side (call when close; first-timers get lost), open since 2017. The chef trained at a famous restaurant. The monthly omakase (¥8,800 or ¥11,000) is Japanese at heart with Western and ethnic twists, from a platter of about ten seasonal small bites to a warm hamo and matsutake bowl in autumn. The fixtures are what bring repeat diners back each month: toro-taku on red-vinegar rice, Saga beef roast beef over achar, a bubbling pot of wagyu with simmered egg, clay-pot rice, and a melting pudding one diner said could rival a dessert shop. Staff suggest sake and wine to match. Report allergies when you book.

chef_bio.background: Creative Japanese restaurant (official site jampa.co.jp; Tabelog). The chef trained at a famous restaurant (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The red vinegar sushi and roast beef are my all-time favorites… The black-haired Wagyu was served with simmered eggs… When the lid of the small pot was lifted, it was bubbling away." — September 2026, seasonal omakase, ninth visit.
"Despite being Japanese cuisine, the addition of ethnic flavors created a perfect balance… The conger eel was served in an ethnic style, wrapped in lettuce." — August 2026.

osaka_men_labo_yuisou_awaza.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–14:30 and 17:00–21:30 (food L.O. 20:30); closing days vary (Tabelog). Order and pay by QR code on your phone (sign-in with Apple or LINE); cash also possible (September 2026). Self-service water. Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_men_labo_yuisou_awaza.notes: [Ramen · light or rich chicken ramen and two-yolk mazesoba by Awaza] A small, clean ramen shop two minutes north of Awaza, open since 2022, where you order and pay on your phone by QR code. The light chicken ramen (¥900) is clear and full-flavored under generous thin-sliced chashu; the rich chicken and pork (¥950) is chicken-led, silky and not greasy despite the name, and you choose thin straight noodles or medium-thick curly hand-kneaded ones. For something different, the tamago-kake mazesoba (¥800) tosses firm flat noodles with two egg yolks and a seafood-flavored sauce. Mix it well. There's also a rich tsukemen on the hand-kneaded noodles, and sea bream bowls come and go. One diner found the phone ordering a hassle when the room was empty.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "Despite being rich, the broth was not overly greasy; it had a clear, silky texture that I really enjoyed!" — August 2026, rich chicken and pork ramen ¥950.
"The flat, medium-thick noodles came with two egg yolks, and the sauce was quite rich, allowing me to enjoy the seafood flavor." — September 2026, tamago-kake mazesoba ¥800.

osaka_ittetsu_kyomachibori.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; soy and shio tare.
osaka_ittetsu_kyomachibori.vegan_detail: Not vegan: niboshi, katsuobushi and sea bream with pork bone; chashu.

Dinner hours may vary (June 2026). Order on a tablet; the bill comes with the food and you pay at a machine at the back (October 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_ittetsu_kyomachibori.notes: [Ramen · niboshi and katsuobushi pork-bone ramen facing Nishisenba Park since 2010] A counter of 14 stylish seats down a small alley in front of Nishisenba Park, near Utsubo Park, running since 2010. Four broths share a pork-bone base: the most popular niboshi ramen (¥900), rich but balanced, with two chashu, half an egg, nori, menma and kaiware included; a rich, creamy katsuobushi seafood ramen that the owner recommends to first-timers; a sea bream shio soba; and a plain chuka soba. One diner of ten years usually orders the plum seafood shio with a free dab of wasabi. A chili-heaped version is milder than it looks. Order on a tablet, pay at the machine at the back. Weekday lunch, dinner on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, until sold out. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth for niboshi ramen is made with niboshi (dried sardines) and pork bone soy sauce, the seafood ramen features katsuobushi (dried bonito) and pork bone soy sauce, the sea bream soba uses sea bream and pork bone salt." — August 2025.
"I usually order the 'Plum Seafood Sio Ramen' with a complimentary topping of wasabi. The consistent deliciousness never gets old." — March 2026, about ten years of visits.

osaka_kokodake_taisho.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: thick wheat noodles; soy tare; ramen tare on the table.
osaka_kokodake_taisho.vegan_detail: Not vegan: tonkotsu-shoyu broth; beef tendon; back fat.
osaka_kokodake_taisho.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:30–14:00 and 17:00–23:30; Sat, Sun and public holidays 11:30–15:00 and 16:00–23:30 (L.O. 23:00); closed the day after a public holiday; hours may change (Tabelog). Call your vegetables, garlic and back fat when the bowl is ready. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_kokodake_taisho.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style ramen with beef tendon instead of pork, by Taisho Station] A Jiro-style shop a minute south of Taisho Station, opened in September 2024 in a former ramen shop, with a Kansai twist: instead of slabs of pork, the beef tendon ramen (¥1,000) comes topped with sweet-savory simmered beef tendon whose collagen melts into a light tonkotsu-shoyu. Call your vegetables, garlic and back fat as usual; it's lighter and easier than most Jiro bowls, so beginners do fine. The show-off topping is Negi Fire, scallions flash-fried tableside with hot onion oil, and you can film it. Spicy garlic chives (¥300) pack a real kick. Change it up midway with the table's pickled ginger or kombu-niboshi vinegar. There's a set with mini curry, and late hours most nights. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Jiro-style ramen shop (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a light tonkotsu soy sauce, paired with thick, chewy noodles… The table condiments included pepper, ramen tare, kombu kelp and niboshi vinegar, chili oil, and pickled ginger." — October 2026, beef tendon noodles ¥1,000.

"The visual impact was impressive, but surprisingly, the taste was much lighter than it looked. However, the umami was rich, and the collagen from the beef tendon melted into the broth." — August 2026, with Negi Fire.

Large noodles free; whether extra vegetables are free or ¥120 differs between the sign and the ticket machine (2025–2026).
osaka_konomen_tamaran_taisho.notes: [Ramen · a lighter Jiro-style ramen with crisp vegetables in Taisho] A small counter near Taisho Station, open since 2015, serving Jiro-style ramen that is gentler than the genre: the broth is light enough to finish, the thick noodles are easy to eat, and the vegetables are blanched for seconds so they stay crisp. The ramen (¥990) comes with free large noodles; call garlic and back fat as you like, and the back fat really gets piled on. One regular wished the garlic and chashu were bolder. Spicy miso is a good variation, and there are Taiwanese mazesoba and tsukemen. Staff are kind and attentive. One diner found it opened at noon, not 11:30. Cash only; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Jiro-style ramen counter (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was surprisingly light and gentle for a Jiro-style ramen. I was able to finish it quite easily." — October 2026.
"The vegetables are pre-packaged, quickly boiled for just a few seconds before serving… the noodles are not overly chewy but rather thick and easy to eat." — October 2026.

One diner found the machine slow to take cash (July 2026). Cards (VISA, Master), IC cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_mazesoba_jujuju_shin_imamiya.notes: [Ramen · seafood mazesoba right by the Nankai gates at Shin-Imamiya] A new, clean noodle shop under Shin-Imamiya Station, steps from the Nankai ticket gates and open 11:00 to 23:00, so it's an easy stop before or after a train. The seafood mazesoba (¥900) mixes chewy noodles with a slightly sweet pork-bone and seafood sauce, egg, diced chashu and fish powder; select rice on the machine if you want to finish the sauce with it, and change it up with the table's kombu vinegar or chili oil. One diner wanted more seafood flavor. The chuka ramen is a nostalgic shoyu, easy to share with a child; staff brought a family separate plates and cups. Kara-age and gyoza fill out the menu. Reviews are mixed: one diner found it mediocre and the machine fussy with cash. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Mazesoba shop at Shin-Imamiya Station (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: "Jumian," noodles from a long-established Shin-Imamiya maker, once made only for celebrations (as described by a July 2026 diner).

anecdotes.text: "The regular size is JPY 900, and the large size is an additional JPY 100. It came with a boiled egg, menma (bamboo shoots), diced chashu (braised pork), fish powder, and green onions… The noodles were chewy." — October 2026, seafood mazesoba.
"The ramen had a nostalgic feel with its soy sauce base, topped with chashu, menma, green onions, and nori—a simple yet satisfying bowl." — July 2026, chuka ramen.

osaka_tori_soba_tori_to_men_taisho.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–14:00 and 17:00–02:00; closing days vary (Tabelog). Lines after Kyocera Dome games; limited chicken paitan often sold out (2025–2026). Self-service water. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_tori_soba_tori_to_men_taisho.notes: [Ramen · parent-chicken shoyu tori soba until 2 am, near Kyocera Dome] A second-floor chicken-ramen counter between Taisho Station and Kyocera Dome, open since 2023 and open until 2 am, so baseball crowds line the stairs after games. One diner traced the style to the nabeyaki ramen of Susaki in Kochi. The tori soba (¥900) is a piping-hot soy broth of long-simmered parent-hen bones with Kochi and Osaka soy and a bright hit of yuzu, on medium-thin straight egg noodles; one diner found the yuzu overpowering. The BLACK version packs garlic and black pepper; RED brings heat; the yuzu shio and a garlicky tori mazesoba fill out the menu. Finish with a chicken chazuke (¥550) or a mini chashu bowl. The limited chicken paitan often sells out. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Chicken ramen shop; Susaki (Kochi) nabeyaki-ramen style, per a June 2026 diner.
chef_bio.philosophy: Broth of parent-chicken bones simmered a long time; tare of Kochi and Osaka soy; served piping hot (June 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a soy sauce base made by simmering chicken bones from parent chickens for a long time. It uses soy sauce from both Kochi and Osaka for the tare, and it is served piping hot." — June 2026, tori soba normal.
"I ordered the Chicken Soba Black for JPY 950… The garlic and black pepper really packed a punch, and the garlic flavor was delicious. It definitely got richer as I continued eating." — July 2025.

osaka_chuka_soba_new_maruchan_doshomachi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–14:00 (L.O. 13:30); closed Sat, Sun and public holidays (Tabelog). A bar at night (April 2026). Ticket machine without pictures; self-service rice bar (2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_chuka_soba_new_maruchan_doshomachi.notes: [Ramen · weekday-lunch chuka soba with ¥250 unlimited mentaiko rice, near Higobashi] A retro-signed, second-floor bar near Higobashi that becomes a ramen shop at weekday lunch. The famous draw is the rice bar: add ¥250 and help yourself to unlimited rice, mentaiko, raw eggs, nori and furikake, and you can order it alone. The chuka soba (¥750) is a sweet, Kyushu-style soy broth on straight noodles that pairs well with all that rice. Heartier options include a back-fat mazesoba with raw egg (¥950, garlic to taste) and the Stanira soba, a spicy, garlicky bowl of garlic chives, chili and ginger. Noodles run soft; one diner plans to ask for them firmer. The ticket machine has no pictures, so decide before the lunch rush. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Bar at night, ramen shop at weekday lunch (April 2026 review; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "For an additional JPY 250, you can enjoy all-you-can-eat rice and mentaiko! There were also raw eggs, furikake, and nori available." — April 2026, back-fat mazesoba ¥950.
"The broth is on the sweeter side. It tastes like a sweet soy sauce from Kyushu. The noodles are straight." — September 2026, chuka soba ¥750.

osaka_hassen_ro_shin_imamiya.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; soy and miso tare; gyoza; fried rice seasoning.
osaka_hassen_ro_shin_imamiya.vegan_detail: Not vegan: tonkotsu broth; back fat; pork-belly chashu.
osaka_hassen_ro_shin_imamiya.hours_raw: Mon, Tue and Thu–Sun 11:00–24:00; closed Wed (Tabelog). Busiest at 22:00–23:00 (2026 reviews). Extra noodles available. Cash only: no cards (Tabelog).
osaka_hassen_ro_shin_imamiya.notes: [Ramen · late-night tonkotsu near Shin-Imamiya and Shinsekai] A thirteen-seat counter a few minutes from Shin-Imamiya, open since 2015 from 11:00 to midnight and packed late in the evening, when it serves as a finishing bowl after a night out. Indian staff keep the room running efficiently. The recommended Tenryu ramen is a rich tonkotsu shoyu with melt-in-the-mouth chashu; the classic bowl floats a layer of fine back fat over a pork-bone soup that is rich but not heavy, with two thick slices of pork belly. The shio tonkotsu is the lighter choice. Pair it with gyoza or the ramen and fried rice set (¥1,150), or order extra noodles. One nine-visit regular says every ramen here is good. Close to Shinsekai and busy with visitors, but not a tourist trap, one diner felt. Cash only; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews). Indian staff keep the room running efficiently (August 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "I tried the recommended Tenryu Ramen, which had a rich tonkotsu soy sauce flavor and melt-in-your-mouth chashu—it was delicious." — September 2026.
"The surface of the broth is generously covered with fine back fat… Surprisingly, it's not too heavy despite its appearance, and the broth has a solid depth and umami." — August 2026, classic ramen.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 八仙楼、大阪市西成区萩之茶屋1-4-1 太陽ビル 1F、南海・JR新今宮駅から徒歩3分、月・火・木〜日 11:00〜24:00、水休み、カード不可、13席、2015年12月10日開店。口コミ(2026年8〜10月): 深夜のラーメン、23時にほぼ満席、アサヒスーパードライの中瓶、塩豚骨ラーメン、どのラーメンもおいしいという声、22時に入店、中華そば、柔らかいチャーシュー、おすすめのTenryuラーメン(濃厚な豚骨醤油、とろけるチャーシュー)、カウンターのみでほぼ満席、飲んだ後の締め、豚骨ラーメンは濃厚、替え玉あり、日曜23時前に3人で、餃子3皿、居酒屋使いも、背脂たっぷりの定番ラーメン、豚骨の旨みと脂の甘み、見た目ほど重くない、厚い豚バラチャーシュー2枚、刻みねぎたっぷり、インバウンド客で混雑、ラーメン炒飯セット1,150円、量が多い、塩豚骨はあっさり、炒飯はやや塩辛め、観光客向けではないという声、味噌ラーメンは濃厚、餃子。

cultural_comfort.note: Busy with visitors near Shinsekai; efficient service (August–September 2026).

osaka_amato_moguraya_nannan.gf_detail: Not gluten-free as a shop: dorayaki and kintsuba use wheat batter or skins, and mitarashi sauce is soy-based. Ask about plain anko, kanten and shiratama.
osaka_amato_moguraya_nannan.vegan_detail: Ask. Dango, anko and kanten have no obvious animal products, but soft serve is dairy and no source lists batter ingredients.
osaka_amato_moguraya_nannan.hours_raw: Daily 10:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:00); closed on NAMBA Nannan's days off (Tabelog). Takeout from 10:00 (March 2026). Eat-in drinks from ¥500 (October 2026). Short waits at busy times; orders taken while you wait (October 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_amato_moguraya_nannan.notes: [Sweets · warm mitarashi dango and dorayaki in the Namba underground mall] A small Japanese-sweets café and takeout counter in the NAMBA Nannan underground mall, connected to Namba Station and open 10:00 to 21:00. The thing to try is mitarashi dango, chewy and served warm in the café, which one diner had never had warm before; to go, it's ¥90 each or three for ¥270. The "Moheji-yaki" dorayaki has a moist, refined batter, the kintsuba lets the azuki speak and can sell out late in the day, and the fukumochi is chewy around chunky red bean. Sitting down, the set B (¥880) gathers warm dango, kinako kanten, anko, shiratama and soft serve, and the mitarashi soft serve pairs warm sauce with cold cream. Expect a short line at busy times. Cards accepted.

chef_bio.background: Japanese sweets café in NAMBA Nannan (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "Includes Mitarashi Dango, agar jelly with kinako, sweet red bean paste, shiratama (rice dumplings), and soft serve ice cream… The Mitarashi Dango was surprisingly warm." — October 2026, set B ¥880.
"The Moheji-yaki is truly the ultimate dorayaki, with a refined flavor in the batter… The Kintsuba… this paste is less sweet, allowing the flavor of the azuki beans to shine through." — April 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 甘党 もぐらや、大阪市中央区難波5丁目 NAMBAなんなん、大阪メトロなんば駅直結、毎日10:00〜21:00(L.O. 20:00)、なんなんに準じて休み、カード可、電子マネー・QR不可、20席。口コミ(2026年3〜10月): 持ち帰りは1本90円・3本270円、店内はドリンク500円から、Moheji-yaki、きんつば、Fukumochiはもちもちの皮につぶあん、きんつばは甘さ控えめで小豆の味、遅いと売り切れ、持ち帰りは10時から、みたらし団子3本270円、パフェ、温かいみたらし団子、ほうじ茶、どら焼きはしっとり、みたらしソフトクリーム、10分待ち、待つ間に注文、おすすめセットB 880円(みたらし団子、きなこの寒天、あんこ、白玉、ソフトクリーム)、平日14時に4人待ち、5分で着席、丁寧で早い接客。

osaka_takekurabe_namba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat-flour batter; yakisoba noodles; okonomiyaki sauces.
osaka_takekurabe_namba.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork, beef tendon, egg; bonito flakes.
osaka_takekurabe_namba.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:00 and 17:00–22:00; Sat–Sun 11:00–22:00; hours may change (Tabelog). Second floor; lines can form at weekend lunch, but seats turn over quickly (2024–2025 reviews). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_takekurabe_namba.notes: [Okonomiyaki · light, fluffy okonomiyaki upstairs by Namba Station] A twelve-seat second-floor okonomiyaki shop a few minutes from Namba Station, cooked on the teppan in front of you. The batter is the point: crisp outside and fluffy within, thick but light, with a sauce that doesn't linger, so you leave without a heavy feeling. One repeat diner always orders the pork modern-yaki with a fried egg before a Shinkigeki show; the suji-negi-tama of slow-cooked beef tendon and green onion is another favorite. Try the house "Take soba," yakisoba wrapped in omelet and pressed. Add the spicy sauce from the table if you like it sharper. Being upstairs, it is easier to get in if you time your visit, one diner notes. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Okonomiyaki restaurant (Tabelog; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "I was amazed by how fluffy the batter was. The outside was perfectly grilled, while the inside was surprisingly soft… Despite its thickness, it didn't feel heavy at all." — September 2026, suji-negi-tama and butatama.
"It was essentially yakisoba wrapped in an omelet and slightly pressed… two types of sauce—spicy and regular—along with mayonnaise and bonito flakes." — May 2026, Take soba.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: たけくらべ、大阪市中央区難波3-2-14、なんばから188m、月〜金 11:00〜15:00・17:00〜22:00、土日 11:00〜22:00、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、12席。口コミ(2024年12月〜2026年9月): 吉本新喜劇の前に、2階なので時間をずらせば待たない、土曜11時40分、ハイボール、豚モダン焼きに卵、いつも同じ注文、後に残らず軽い、帰りに行列、ソースとマヨネーズは追加も可、待てば席がすぐ空く、Take soba(焼きそばを卵で包んで軽く押さえたもの)、ソースは辛口と普通、マヨネーズ、かつお節、ラーメンのような少し平たい麺、水をよく気にかけてくれる、すじ焼き、たたみ焼きそば、接客が気になったという声、平日18時に待たずに入店、一品料理も多い、ふわふわの生地、すじねぎ玉、豚玉、目玉焼きのせ、ミックス焼き、鉄板で目の前で焼く、なんば駅近く。

osaka_shunsen_waraku_sanai.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: a set kaiseki course built on dashi and soy seasoning; no gluten-free course is listed.
osaka_shunsen_waraku_sanai.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi throughout; seafood such as conger eel and abalone in the course.
osaka_shunsen_waraku_sanai.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 18:00–22:00 (L.O. 20:30); closed Mon and some other days; call about later arrivals (official site). Tabelog lists 18:00–22:30 (food L.O. 20:00). Courses only; à la carte suspended (Tabelog). Children only if ordering the same course (official site). Prices revised from 1 October 2026 (official site). Cards (VISA, Master, AMEX, JCB, Diners); no e-money (official site).
osaka_shunsen_waraku_sanai.notes: [Japanese · seasonal Kansai kaiseki at a pine counter since 2005, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A calm, sukiya-style kappo near Nipponbashi, open since 2005, serving kaiseki courses only, built on seasonal ingredients from the Kinki region and a gentle, deep dashi. Sit at the five-seat counter of single-board pine to watch the cooking, or take the horigotatsu tatami room. Dishes arrive in seasonal tableware with matching chopstick rests, and the sake list is wide; ask for pairings. The menu follows what's good that day, so one diner who booked expecting matsutake and turtle got conger eel and abalone instead. Rice comes with refills. Diners spent about ¥15,000–30,000, and the shop raised some prices in October 2026 for matsutake and crab. Children only with the same course.

chef_bio.background: Kappo serving kaiseki courses (official site shunsenwaraku-sanai.com; Tabelog).
chef_bio.philosophy: Kaiseki built on the five flavors, colors, senses and methods; Kinki-region seasonal ingredients in their early, peak and late stages; dishes adjusted to guests' requests (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The seasonal chopstick rests and tableware added to the visual delight of the experience. I also appreciated the variety of Japanese sake available." — May 2025.
"Each dish is crafted with great care, and the dashi (broth) was incredibly delicious and gentle in flavor. The service was excellent." — January 2026.

osaka_baniku_kigokoro_higashi_shinsaibas.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: soy-based dips for the sashimi; soba and nyumen finishes; gyoza.
osaka_baniku_kigokoro_higashi_shinsaibas.vegan_detail: Not vegan: horse meat in nearly every dish; dashi.
osaka_baniku_kigokoro_higashi_shinsaibas.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–24:00 (L.O. 23:00); closed Sun (Tabelog). Smoking allowed, so no one under 20 (Tabelog). Reservations held 10 minutes; Friday and Saturday often full, so book ahead (2025–2026 reviews). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_baniku_kigokoro_higashi_shinsaibas.notes: [Horse meat · basashi and horse shabu-shabu in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A horse-meat specialist set back in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building behind a noren, open since 2020, with a narrow counter by the kitchen and tables further in. The meat is sourced direct from producers, and diners remark on how clean it tastes, with none of the usual odor. Start with the assorted basashi, five kinds or seven with heart and tongue, from lean thigh and tenderloin to the rich mane fat, then a sakura yukhoe or tataki. On a cold night, the horse shabu-shabu is the warming choice, finished with unusually thick, soft soba; skewers come each with its own salt or sauce. One diner comes almost monthly and books Friday and Saturday well ahead. Smoking is allowed, so no one under 20.

chef_bio.background: Horse-meat specialist (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Horse meat sourced directly from producers (April 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "Every dish was free of the typical horse meat odor, allowing me to savor an astonishingly clear umami and sweetness. The freshness of the sashimi was particularly outstanding." — February 2026.
"I indulged in the hot pot (Dashi Shabu) after a long time, finishing off with soba. The thick and soft texture of the soba is quite unique." — December 2025.

osaka_kappou_uosaki_higashi_shinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: an omakase of about 20 dashi- and soy-seasoned dishes; dislikes are asked in advance, but no gluten-free option is described.
osaka_kappou_uosaki_higashi_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seafood-led omakase; fugu or duck hot pot.
osaka_kappou_uosaki_higashi_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Hours not listed on Tabelog. Omakase course only; reserve, as it is full most days (April 2026). Smoking allowed (June 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money (Tabelog).
osaka_kappou_uosaki_higashi_shinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · kappo omakase of about twenty small dishes in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A hidden kappo in a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, often fully booked, that serves one thing: an omakase of about twenty small dishes in little bowls, each prettily presented, with grilling done in front of you at the counter. Diners rate the grilled dishes highly, and one remembers the firefly squid. The seasoning leans a little strong, which one diner says makes the sake go down easily. In autumn the finish is a fugu or duck hot pot with matsutake, its broth poured over matsutake rice. There's a wide sake and shochu list, with recommendations if you ask. Expect about ¥10,000–15,000. Hours aren't published, so call to book. Smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: Kappo restaurant (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The meal consists of about 20 small dishes, all of which are delicious and enjoyable." — March 2026; omakase only, with dislikes asked first.
"For the final course, we could choose between fugu or duck hot pot… The way to finish off the meal was to pour the hot pot broth over the matsutake rice." — October 2025.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 割烹 魚先、大阪市中央区東心斎橋1-15-11 日宝周防町エレガンスビル 1F、心斎橋駅6番出口から徒歩4分、長堀橋から5分、カード可、電子マネー不可、16席(カウンター6、テーブル10)、予算10,000〜14,999円、営業時間の記載なし。口コミ(2025年10月〜2026年6月): メニューはなくコースのみ、小鉢がいくつも、焼き物が香ばしい、締めはふぐか鴨の鍋、松茸・あさり・豚を加えて、鍋の出汁を松茸ご飯にかける、ミナミの有名な割烹、やさしい味、日本酒と焼酎が豊富、ほたるいかの焼き物、落ち着いた雰囲気、おまかせのみ、最初に苦手なものを確認、約20品の小皿、地酒はやや高め、小鉢に盛られた料理、盛り付けが美しい、ほぼ毎日満席で予約必須、全体にやや濃い味、日本酒のおすすめ、目の前で焼く、喫煙可。

osaka_chuka_soba_try_tennoji.notes: [Ramen · late-night Takaida-style dark shoyu on thick noodles, near Tennoji] A one-person chuka soba counter on Tanimachi-suji a short walk from Tennoji, open from 19:00 to 03:00, a natural stop after a night out. It serves Takaida-style ramen, the Osaka and Higashi-Osaka genre: a dark, clear soy broth and thick straight noodles with real chew, under chashu, menma and green onion cut in big, crunchy pieces. The chuka soba is ¥700 and the chashu ramen ¥900 with generous slices. Diners differ on the broth: some find it punchy, one found it milder than it looks, another lukewarm, with tough chashu. Grab a rice ball from the counter, and help yourself to a canned beer. The owner is cheerful. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Late-night ramen counter run by one person (May 2026 review; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The standout features are the 'rich soy sauce' and 'thick noodles!' The dark broth has a clear soy sauce flavor… The thick noodles have a satisfying chewiness." — August 2026.
"The noodles are thick and quite filling. The green onions are cut into larger pieces, which pair well with the broth. The chashu was generously served and delicious." — October 2026, chashu ramen.

Busy after Kyocera Dome games (September 2026). Choose garlic (none, a little, a lot) and noodle firmness. AMEX, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_mentomi_tenyo_kujo.notes: [Ramen · garlic tonkotsu shoyu almost all night, by Kyocera Dome] The Kujo shop of the Tenyo garlic-ramen family, open since 1988 and now renovated and renamed from "Garlic Ramen Tenyo," serving from 11:00 straight through to 05:00 or 06:00. It fills after Kyocera Dome games. The ramen (¥1,100) is a surprisingly light tonkotsu shoyu that the garlic transforms: ask for none, a little or a lot, and stir it up from the bottom. The chashu is slow-cooked domestic pork so soft it falls apart, and it's even better shredded in sweet-spicy sauce over the B-set rice bowl (¥450, large free). The menu now runs to miso, a negi ramen, a tangy W vinegar ramen, curry noodles and tsukemen. One diner found the noodles clumped. Tenyo's Shinmachi and Taishobashi shops are also in this guide.

chef_bio.background: Garlic ramen shop of the Tenyo name, formerly "Garlic Ramen Tenyo" (October 2026 review; official site tenyou.jp).

anecdotes.text: "The light tonkotsu soy sauce broth pairs perfectly with the medium-thin curly noodles… Slow-cooked domestic pork that has a melt-in-your-mouth texture, reminiscent of kakuni." — September 2026, ramen ¥1,100.
"The name has also changed from 'Garlic Ramen Tenyo' to just 'Tenyo.' That said, the garlic ramen is still the highlight… options like miso ramen, tsukemen, and curry." — October 2026.

osaka_gyukotsu_ramen_bukkoshi_kitahama.vegan_detail: Not vegan: beef-bone broth; beef-belly chashu; egg.
osaka_gyukotsu_ramen_bukkoshi_kitahama.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–14:30 and 17:30–22:45; closed Sat–Sun (Tabelog). One diner found it open on a Sunday via the shop's Instagram (October 2026). Ticket machine; self-service water. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_gyukotsu_ramen_bukkoshi_kitahama.notes: [Ramen · creamy beef-bone paitan ramen from ¥850 in Kitahama] A small weekday counter in Kitahama serving gyukotsu ramen, a white soup slow-simmered from beef bones, part of a family of beef-bone shops. It looks like tonkotsu but tastes lighter and gentler, creamy without dairy, so you'll likely finish the soup. The basic bowl with a soft-boiled egg is only ¥850; the extra-meat version (¥1,250) piles on thin, flavorful beef-belly chashu, and pea shoots and baby corn keep it fresh. The spicy version (¥1,100) brings real heat without hiding the beef. Noodles are homemade and straight, a bit firm. Add lunch rice for ¥100 or a roast beef rice bowl. One diner found the chashu tired one day. Weekdays only per Tabelog; cash only.

chef_bio.background: Beef-bone ramen shop, Kitahama branch, part of a group of beef-bone ramen shops (September 2026 review; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The distinctive feature of this ramen is the white broth, slowly simmered from beef bones. The rich umami of the beef is concentrated yet not overpowering, and the texture is creamy." — October 2026, extra-meat gyukotsu paitan ¥1,250.
"At first glance, the soup looks like a traditional tonkotsu ramen, but in reality, it's creamy yet light and very easy to drink, with a gentle flavor." — October 2026, gyukotsu paitan with egg ¥850.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 牛骨ら～めん ぶっこ志 北浜店、大阪市中央区道修町1-5-12、北浜駅から徒歩5分、月〜金 11:00〜14:30・17:30〜22:45、土日休み、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター11席、2016年7月11日開店。口コミ(2026年9〜10月): 牛骨スープの専門店、Kokorozashiグループの系列という声、辛い牛白湯の味玉1,100円、クリーミーなスープと辛さのバランス、食券制、水はセルフ、カウンター約8席という声、白濁したスープ、チャーシュー2枚、白髪ねぎ、豆苗、麺は少し固め、肉増し牛骨白湯1,250円、ランチの白ご飯100円、牛バラのチャーシュー、ヤングコーン、自家製のストレート麺、日曜にInstagramで営業を確認、乳製品を使わず軽いのにコク、焼豚丼は売り切れでローストビーフご飯、チャーシューに臭みがあったという声、牛骨白湯ラーメン(味玉)850円、飲んだ後にも。

osaka_mabo_club_higobashi.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–14:30 and 17:30–22:00; hours may change (Tabelog). Lunch waits of about 10 minutes (August 2026). Ticket machine; paper aprons. Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_mabo_club_higobashi.notes: [Ramen · mapo mazesoba under a giant fried-to-order katsu, near Higobashi] A stylish, black-themed counter near Higobashi, open since 2024, whose signature is built for photos: a mapo mazesoba hidden under a chicken-thigh katsu so large it covers the bowl. Mix the noodles through the thick mapo first; it's rich with sweet bean sauce and a Sichuan-pepper tingle rather than fiery, and the katsu, fried to order, stays crisp in the sauce. Pick from five heat levels (three free); level 3 is sweat-inducing, one diner warns. A mini rice comes on the side to dive into the leftovers. The bowl now runs ¥1,600 after a price rise, and it's a lot of food. There's also a mapo rice, cold noodles in summer and a weekly set. Expect a short wait at lunch. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Mapo-noodle shop, Higobashi branch (official site mabo-club.com; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "This isn't the typical Mabo Noodles with the tofu floating in the broth; it's a Mazesoba style where the noodles are coated in the Mabo tofu… a thick, rich type with a strong flavor of sweet bean sauce." — August 2026, chicken katsu mabo noodles ¥1,400.
"Each katsu is fried to order, with an astonishingly crispy coating that bursts with juicy meat. Even when submerged in the rich Mabo sauce, its light and crispy texture remains intact." — May 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式 mabo-club.com。食べログ: 麻婆倶楽部 肥後橋店、大阪市西区江戸堀1-20-4、肥後橋から288m、毎日11:00〜14:30・17:30〜22:00、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、2024年5月14日開店。口コミ(2026年5〜10月): 揚げたての大きなとんかつをのせた麻婆麺、花椒の香り、辛さ2で痺れ、辛さは5段階、チキンカツ麻婆麺、辛さ3は汗だくになるという声、昼は10分待ち、辛い冷麺の大盛り(夏)、チキンカツ麻婆麺1,400円(8月)、黒いエプロン、ミニご飯付き、まずよく混ぜるまぜそばスタイル、甜麺醤の濃い麻婆、チキンカツ麻婆飯1,200円、週替わりの定食、カウンターが多く一人でも、清潔、黒基調のおしゃれな店内、3人で営業、カウンターとテーブル、チキンカツ麻婆麺(辛さ2)1,600円、辛さ3まで無料、中太のもちもちの麺、ダイブめし付き、最近値上げ。

osaka_densho_aburasoba_kobuta_no_hana.notes: [Ramen · abura soba by Kitahama, mixed from the bottom] A small, bright and clean abura soba shop between Kitahama and Yodoyabashi, open since 2018, busy at office lunch. The house Densho abura soba (¥890) is slightly spicy: smooth curly noodles coated in a moderately rich sauce under thin-sliced chashu and a pile of white negi. The wall sign says to mix everything thoroughly from the bottom, and the noodles turn chewy as you do. If you don't want heat, the chicken-negi abura soba (¥960) is mild and light. A shrimp shio version comes with rare chashu, and there's a light chicken shio soup ramen. Tune it with the vinegar, chili oil and garlic chips on the table. A ¥1,300 drink set adds menma and a menchi-katsu. Cash-only ticket machine; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Abura soba shop (Tabelog; Facebook page yamabuta.zing).

anecdotes.text: "The abura-soba features a moderately rich broth that perfectly coats the smooth, curly noodles. Plus, it's topped generously with spicy green onions, which is simply fantastic." — October 2026.

"According to a paper on the wall, you should mix everything thoroughly from the bottom, including the chashu… Mine was completely non-spicy and quite light, making it easy to eat." — October 2026, chicken-negi abura soba ¥960.

osaka_menya_ageha_otedori.notes: [Ramen · rich tonkotsu-seafood tsukemen and two mazesoba near Tenmabashi] A thirteen-seat shop under a black and red sign between Tenmabashi and Tanimachi 4-chome, open since 2013, that fills up by noon. The draw for many is the rich tonkotsu tsukemen: thick, smooth, chewy noodles in a rich yet clean seafood and pork dip with chopped onion and thick grilled chashu, large at no extra cost. A repeat diner, though, swears by the mazesoba: choose shoyu (seafood-soy sauce, cheese, nori, flat chewy noodles) or curry (¥1,150, minced meat, garlic chives and a raw egg), and you'll be asked which when you hand over the ticket. Finish by tipping the small yuzu-kosho rice into the leftovers with a splash of dashi. One diner found the chashu a little salty. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen and tsukemen shop (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The Tsukemen was a typical 'Mata oma kei' style with a rich seafood and pork bone broth… The noodles were especially smooth and chewy." — August 2026.
"The soy sauce sauce has a seafood flavor, topped with grilled chashu, green onions, cheese, and nori! The noodles are wonderfully flat and chewy!" — August 2026, shoyu mazesoba, fourth visit.

osaka_ramen_agein_kitahama.notes: [Ramen · morning-to-lunch shoyu and spicy miso by Kitahama Station] An eight-seat counter a minute from Kitahama Station, open since 2024 and opening as early as 10:00 for a breakfast or early-lunch bowl, and a line can form by 11:00. The common thread is grilled chashu of branded pork, charred and fragrant, praised by several diners. The shoyu ramen (¥1,100) is light, with a sharp soy and clean umami; diners split on it, from refreshing to too plain and sour. The spicy miso (¥1,380) builds on pork and scallop broth with a house miso and a spicy powder to stir in, and the black wagyu kamadama niku niku (¥1,000), found in a binder rather than on the ticket machine, ends with a raw egg and soy over the last noodles. Hours vary; check Instagram. Cash only; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter; Instagram @ramen_again_osaka, X @Ramen_again (Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Shoyu and spicy miso ramen with grilled chashu.

anecdotes.text: "I ordered the Spicy Miso Ramen for JPY 1380, made with Kurabio pork and scallop broth, along with homemade miso sauce… The chashu on the far left was freshly grilled and had a great texture." — October 2026.
"The soy sauce flavor was sharp, but the first bite was all about the aroma of the broth!… The chashu was grilled, which added an incredible fragrance." — October 2026, spicy shoyu ramen.

osaka_temmabashi_sasara.notes: [Ramen · golden-sesame tantanmen near Tenmabashi] A twelve-seat tantanmen counter near Tenmabashi with a regular who has logged 17 visits and can't go two weeks without it. The kin-goma tantanmen (¥980) is the order: a thick, creamy, sesame-forward soup that's easy to drink, somewhere between soup and dry tantanmen, over thin noodles with minced meat and a good amount of vegetables. Pick a heat level, with three free; level 3 makes the lips tingle. The ritual is the finish: add set A (¥170) and tip the rice and kimchi into the last of the soup like a porridge, with more ground sesame and Sichuan pepper from the table. At lunch, large noodles are free. A chilled tantanmen appears in summer. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Tantanmen shop (official site sasala.jp; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "After slurping the noodles, I did my usual routine of diving rice and kimchi into the soup, then sprinkled some ground sesame and Sichuan pepper on top." — August 2025, kin-goma tantanmen with set A.

"The soup… had a strong sesame aroma and richness. The broth was not too thin, nor too thick, but rather creamy and easy to drink. The noodles were thin and paired well." — October 2026, kin-goma tantanmen ¥980.

osaka_unagi_shi_gensai.notes: [Eel · crisp, unsteamed eel courses with eel shabu-shabu, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] An eight-seat eel counter on a second floor in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, opened at the end of August 2026 and on some days already booked from noon to close. Live eels are prepared on the spot and grilled Kansai-style without steaming over fierce heat, so the skin comes out crisp, like a potato chip in the shirayaki, while the flesh stays fluffy and juicy. The ¥7,700 course walks through it all: a creamy yuba sesame tofu, rare eel shabu-shabu in ponzu, crisp shirayaki and kabayaki side by side, then an unaju of a whole eel with liver soup; three kinds of sansho let you play with the finish. A ¥4,800 unadon is the shorter route. Call ahead for red-vinegar sushi. Diners compare it favorably with Japan's best eel shops. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Eel restaurant (Tabelog; September–October 2026 reviews).
chef_bio.philosophy: Live eels prepared to order; no steaming, grilled over strong heat for crisp skin and fluffy flesh (October 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "By skipping the steaming process… the skin is crispy while the inside remains juicy and rich in flavor… You can enjoy the crispy unaju, the rare 'unagi shabu-shabu,' and even sushi." — October 2026.

"The shirayaki (grilled unagi without sauce) was as crispy as potato chips and absolutely delicious… The kabayaki (grilled unagi with sauce) was not crispy but rather fluffy and moist." — September 2026, unadon ¥4,800.

osaka_sushi_higuchi_higashi_shinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · high-end sushi ordered your way near Nagahoribashi, since 2009] An eight-seat counter near Nagahoribashi, open since 2009 and on Tabelog's sushi 100 in 2022, that breaks the high-end sushi mold: there's no fixed course or common start time. Small dishes are shown at the counter and you pick what you like, then grilled fish, sashimi and nigiri as you please, so light drinkers can go straight to sushi and sake lovers can linger. The rice is pressed so gently that it settles under the topping, and one diner singles out a surprising shiitake nigiri and crisp-skinned eel. The chef keeps the room lively and picks sake to match. Expect ¥15,000–30,000. One diner has come for 24 years. Closed Thursday and Sunday; last entry 20:30.

osaka_ryota_higashi_shinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · one-chef creative washoku counter by Shinsaibashi] A quiet counter of six to eight seats on the fourth floor of a building a minute from Shinsaibashi, open since 2024 and run by a single chef who cooks, serves and watches over every guest. A young chef opened this eight-seat counter after seven years at a Michelin two-star restaurant. The cooking is refined rather than flashy: the seven-dish course with drinks (¥11,000) runs from a mizuna and beef appetizer through a sashimi platter with sea urchin and crab, a chewy lotus-root dumpling in kuzu sauce and Saikyo-grilled flounder to seasonal tempura and a clay-pot rice, with leftovers turned into onigiri for tomorrow. À la carte, diners praise the firm tuna, very fresh sea urchin and a precisely cooked steak. The sake list is broad. Open late, and on Sunday nights when much of Minami is closed. Heated tobacco only.

osaka_izakaya_odashi_higashi_shinsaibash.notes: [Izakaya · oden and sake by Nagahoribashi] A modern, lively oden izakaya in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2020, where the counter lets you watch the cooking and it's often fully booked, even on a rainy Monday. Three young men run it, with refreshing service. The house dashi is a blend built on the taste of the long-established 神楽; diners call it fresh and deep, though one wanted it stronger. The oden is playfully cut, with a star in the daikon and tofu scored like sea anemones; one diner had never understood shungiku in oden until it arrived here, steeped and fragrant. The sashimi is serious, there's gyoza and fried food, and the sake list is long. Service is quick and friendly. Note the ¥600 seat charge, the two-hour limit, and that smoking is allowed.

chef_bio.background: Oden izakaya (official site izakaya-odashi.com; Tabelog). Three young men run it, with refreshing service (September 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: House dashi blended on the base of the taste of the long-established 神楽 (official site).

anecdotes.text: "The shungiku here is incredibly delicious. Soaked in the broth, it comes out as if to say, 'I'm the star of the show from today on.'… Additionally, the sashimi is genuinely good." — September 2026.
"I noticed some creative touches, like the daikon radish being cut into a star shape in the center and the tofu having cuts resembling sea anemones." — September 2026.

osaka_oshokuji_dokoro_imachan.notes: [Izakaya · one-person Showa-retro izakaya deep in Jumbo Yokocho] A tiny, warm counter at the back of the neon-lit Jumbo Yokocho alley in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, run single-handed since 2009 by a friendly owner. It feels straight out of the Showa era: cheap, homemade dishes like natto-yaki, pork kimchi, butter-fried itawasa and edamame, nikujaga and chikuzen-ni, and drinks poured famously strong, with shochu and green tea at about seven to three. Order a few dishes at a time, since one person cooks everything; customers end up helping each other out and chatting, which is half the charm. The entrance is easy to miss, so allow time to find it. Open until 2 am most nights. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Izakaya run by one person (2017–2026 reviews; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "It's a mysterious space where customers naturally cooperate and care for each other, creating a sense of teamwork as soon as you step inside." — February 2026.
"…First off, the drinks are strong! Haha. The shochu with green tea is about 70% shochu and 30% green tea." — February 2026.

osaka_tori_soba_zagin_honten.notes: [Ramen · whipped chicken paitan with fried burdock, on Tabelog's Ramen 100 since 2020, Higobashi] The original Zagin, a twelve-seat counter two minutes from Higobashi and on Tabelog's Ramen 100 every year from 2020 to 2025. The tori soba (¥1,000) is a chicken paitan whipped to a creamy froth before it's served, on thin straight noodles with low-temperature chicken and pork chashu and a tangle of fried burdock that turns from crunchy to soft as it soaks (one diner found the burdock missing on one visit); an eleven-visit regular calls it a favorite ramen in Osaka. There's a shoyu version and a chicken tsuke soba with a thick, concentrated dip; one regular found the rich shio and the shoyu less special than the original. Buy a ticket outside, then queue; staff are calm and polite. Open 10:30 to 22:30 every day. Cash only. The Niboshi branch is also in this guide.

chef_bio.background: Main branch of the Zagin chicken-ramen shops; Tabelog Ramen 100 (WEST 2020–2022, OSAKA 2023–2025) (Tabelog; official site silver-grape.com).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles are thin, cooked perfectly without being overdone. The broth is whipped before serving… There are two slices of chashu (chicken and pork), both cooked at low temperatures." — October 2026, chicken shio soba ¥1,000.
"The creamy, frothy soup was consistently delicious, and the fried burdock root topping added a fun twist… it transitioned from crunchy to soft as it soaked in the broth." — October 2026.

osaka_tai_tanmen_dakishimetai.notes: [Ramen · sea bream tantanmen with a tai-meshi finish, near Higobashi] A popular tantanmen shop near Higobashi, open since 2018, which one review describes as crossing Japanese sea bream dashi, Sichuan tantanmen and French technique. The tai tanmen was created by a chef with 12 years in French cuisine. The tai tanmen (¥960) is a creamy soup of Uwajima sea bream and sesame, heat and numbing to order (level 2 is moderate, level 3 genuinely hot), over chewy wavy noodles with meat miso, rare chashu, mizuna and shredded fried potato. Order the set with tai-meshi (¥1,200): eat some plain, add soup for a risotto, then pour on the free tai dashi for ochazuke. A soupless version and a ¥1,600 monthly special, such as crab and porcini bisque, keep one four-visit diner coming back. One diner barely tasted the sea bream in the noodles, but loved the rice. Buy a ticket and expect a short line after 11:30.

chef_bio.background: Tai tanmen specialist (official site taitanmendakishimetai.com; Tabelog). The tai tanmen was created by a chef with 12 years in French cuisine (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Japanese sea bream dashi with Sichuan dandan noodles and French techniques; Uwajima sea bream (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The soup is a spicy broth based on sea bream, paired with medium-thick wavy noodles. The toppings include meat miso, mizuna greens, pork and chicken chashu, menma (bamboo shoots), and shredded fried potatoes." — October 2026, tai tanmen level 2 ¥960.
"I enjoyed it in three stages: first as is, then adding the soup for a risotto-like experience, and finally pouring the Tai broth over it for a delightful ochazuke." — October 2026, tai-meshi set.

osaka_ramen_three_higobashi.notes: [Ramen · clam-broth ramen with three kinds of chashu, by Higobashi] A quiet, café-like ramen shop a minute from Higobashi, open since 2022, built on clam broth. The owner trained at Kaimen Mikawa in Shimokitazawa, Tokyo. The clam ramen comes clear and light in shio or shoyu, rich in shellfish umami, over thin noodles with crunchy chopped onion, thick menma and three kinds of low-temperature chashu; one repeat diner, after trying everything, still names the clam and Kyoto bonito chuka soba (special ¥1,150) the one everyone will like. At lunch any rice is ¥100: take the clam rice and pour the last of the soup over it as chazuke. Seasonal bowls rotate, from Ise lobster with truffle butter to chilled oyster and the cold Suriyan with two egg yolks. One diner found the plain clam ramen monotonous. Expect a short wait at weekday noon. Cards and QR accepted.

chef_bio.background: Clam-broth ramen shop (official site ramenthree.com; Tabelog). The owner trained at Kaimen Mikawa in Shimokitazawa, Tokyo (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The three types of chashu are cooked at low temperatures, making them thick and moist, while the thin noodles pair well with the clear broth, allowing you to enjoy the lightness typical of shio ramen along with the rich umami of the shellfish." — October 2026, special clam ramen ¥1,200.

"After finishing the noodles, I poured the leftover soup over the Finishing Clam Rice. It turned into a clam broth chazuke, and the flavors of the asari (clam) tsukudani, rice crackers, seaweed, and rice filled my mouth." — October 2026, Suriyan ¥1,000.

osaka_kozou_mata_omae_ka_tosabori.notes: [Ramen · fish-powder tonkotsu-gyokai ramen and mazesoba, large free, near Higobashi] A thirteen-seat branch of the Kozou ramen shops on the Edobori side of Higobashi, open daily since 2021, and one diner's monthly habit. The Kozou ramen (¥1,000) is a thick, creamy tonkotsu-seafood soup heaped with fish powder, rich but not heavy enough to stop you finishing it; the large size costs nothing extra. The tonkotsu-gyokai mazesoba (¥1,150), billed as the most popular, gets the same fish powder with egg, chashu and chopped onion; mix it well from the bottom and add garlic from the table. One diner found the mazesoba a bit sweet and preferred the ramen. Seasonal specials rotate, from a chilled negi chuka to a chashu zaru chuka with up to 350 g of free noodles. Open 11:00 to 22:00 every day; PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Tosabori branch of the Kozou ramen shops (official site kozou53.jp; October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "Packed with fish powder, the rich tonkotsu broth is thick and creamy, yet not heavy at all! Before I knew it, I had finished the entire bowl of soup!" — September 2026, Kozou ramen ¥1,000.
"I mixed it well to coat everything with the rich sauce, and it was a real treat. The egg and chashu (braised pork) were both incredibly satisfying." — October 2026, tonkotsu-gyokai mazesoba ¥1,150.

osaka_kitahama_nikaku_shokudo.notes: [Ramen · Niigata-style back-fat niboshi chuka soba in Kitahama] A thirteen-seat counter a few minutes from Kitahama, reopened in March 2026 with a new name and menu, serving a style that one diner calls hard to find in Osaka: Niigata back-fat niboshi chuka soba. The bowl (¥1,140 with a seasoned egg) is a pork clear soup with a strong niboshi hit and soy, buried in back fat, minced onion and iwanori seaweed, over thick, wavy, low-hydration noodles you chew more than slurp, under a big, tender slice of pork-shoulder chashu. A plainer chuka soba (¥890) comes light or rich. Add the chashu-egg rice bowl (¥500). The broth can run salty; one diner couldn't finish it one day. Open until 00:30 on weeknights. Cards and IC accepted.

chef_bio.origin: Reopened 2 March 2026 under this name, formerly "Niboshi Chuka Soba Kourai no Hishou" (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

"I took a sip of the clear broth topped with a generous amount of back fat… It has a seafood soy sauce flavor based on pork bone. The distinctive noodles are thick, curly noodles made by 'Menya Teigaku' in Kyoto." — October 2026, chuka soba ¥890.

Usually run by one person, so waits when busy (August 2026). Order and pay in cash first (2026). No cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Specials announced by SMS.
osaka_kujo_manten.notes: [Ramen · clear jidori shoyu and shio, and inventive summer chilled bowls, by Kujo] A small, slightly hidden counter three minutes from Kujo, open since 2023 and usually run by one cook who chats with guests and has adjusted a recipe in response to guest feedback. The owner previously ran Naniwa Tonkotsu Ramen Taisho Bashi Manten near Taisho Station before going independent. The broth is a clear soup of Tajima chicken and Tanba black chicken with real kombu and a delicate seafood dashi; the shoyu ramen is deep enough to drink to the last drop, with firm straight noodles and pink rare chashu. Pair it with the tamago-kake gohan, made with a branded egg. Summer brings the stars: a chilled shio ramen (¥1,200) with tomato ice cubes and two chashu, and a weekend chilled hamo ramen with sudachi, best tried on the spoon first. With one person cooking, expect waits when it's busy. Order and pay in cash up front.

chef_bio.background: Clear-broth ramen shop usually run by one person (August 2026 review; Tabelog). The owner previously ran Naniwa Tonkotsu Ramen Taisho Bashi Manten near Taisho Station before going independent (July 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: Tajima chicken, Tanba black chicken and real kombu; noodles made with a Kyoto (Teigaku) vacuum mixer (August 2026 review).
chef_bio.specialty: Clear-broth shoyu and shio; chilled ramen.

anecdotes.text: "The broth, rich with the concentrated umami of free-range chicken, combined with a delicate seafood dashi and the depth of soy sauce, creates an incredibly delicious experience… The beautifully pink rare chashu is moist and tender." — August 2026, shoyu ramen.

"It featured medium-thick straight noodles, three slices of rare chashu, three slices of chicken chashu, finely chopped onions, half a seasoned egg, three tomato-flavored ice cubes, menma, green onions, and yuzu." — August 2026, chilled shio ramen ¥1,200.

osaka_menya_taka_tosabori.notes: [Ramen · clear niboshi chuka soba on homemade flat noodles, by Awaza] A one-person, eleven-seat L-shaped counter near Awaza, open since 2016, where "simple is best": the chuka soba (¥1,000) is a beautifully clear soy broth of chicken bones, pork bones and niboshi on homemade flat, straight, high-hydration noodles that are smooth with a wheat aroma, topped with thin chashu and chopped onion, which reminds one diner of Hachioji ramen. Add pepper to sharpen it. For a change, the TKM mixes those flat noodles with niboshi broth and two eggs, and there's a shio, a mazemen and a tantanmen. Fried rice (¥500) and a small rice bowl round it out. Firmness can't be chosen, and the shop sometimes closes early. Cash only; closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter run by one person (June 2026 review; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "Soup: A clear soy sauce broth made from chicken bones, pork bones, and niboshi (dried sardines). The noodles are medium-sized, flat, and straight with a smooth texture." — May 2026, chuka soba ¥1,000.
"The noodles are homemade, medium-thick, and flat. They have a lovely wheat aroma and a smooth texture… With chopped onions mixed in, it might remind you of Hachioji ramen." — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 麺屋 TAKA、大阪市西区土佐堀3-3-21、阿波座から491m、月・火・木〜日 11:30〜14:30・18:00〜22:00、水休み、早じまいあり、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター11席、2016年3月14日開店。口コミ(2024年10月〜2026年8月): 中華そば1,000円、阿波座駅9番出口から徒歩約6分、鶏ガラ・豚骨・煮干しの澄んだ醤油スープ、中くらいの平打ちストレート麺、硬さは選べない、薄いチャーシュー4枚、刻み玉ねぎ、ねぎ、L字のカウンター約10席、多加水のなめらかな麺、玉子かけ麺(TKM)1,000円(卵2個、煮干しの香り)、担々麺、まぜ麺、塩930円(2024年)、2種のチャーシュー、中華そばと炒飯500円、ランチメニューなし、ワンオペ、ミニ丼は「Hashi Niku Don」に、醤油ラーメン大盛りに味玉、やさしいスープ、シンプルが一番、煮干しのあっさりスープ、胡椒で味が締まる、自家製の中太平打ち麺、小麦の香り、刻み玉ねぎで八王子ラーメンのよう。

osaka_buta_ni_naru_edobori.vegan_detail: Not vegan: pork broth; back fat; pork chashu; egg.
osaka_buta_ni_naru_edobori.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:30) and 18:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:30); hours may change (Tabelog). Buy a ticket and enter in order; no Jiro-style call needed (2026). Rarely a wait at lunch (September 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_buta_ni_naru_edobori.notes: [Ramen · beginner-friendly Jiro-style ramen in Edobori] A thirteen-seat counter near Higobashi, open since November 2024, serving Jiro-style ramen without the rituals: you buy a ticket, enter in order and skip the topping call. The standard 200 g bowl has a sharp soy flavor balanced by the sweetness of noodles and vegetables, which go up to double-extra; the fat is unseasoned, so eat it with the noodles, and the pork is firm and lean. The soupless ramen (¥1,100) is a repeat diner's order, the cold TKM coats the noodles in egg, and the soupless tantanmen with an onsen egg is properly spicy. Pile on mayonnaise, pork scraps or a raw egg if you want the full effect. Lunch rarely has a wait. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Jiro-style ramen shop; Instagram @butaninaru1 (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The flavor is characterized by a sharp soy sauce taste. The sweetness from the noodles and vegetables balances it out nicely. The fat is unseasoned, so it's better enjoyed together with the noodles and broth." — September 2026, ramen 200 g.
"It operates on a ticket system, has no special ordering calls, making it beginner-friendly." — October 2026, soupless ramen 200 g ¥1,100.

osaka_sushi_shizuku_shinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: house sauces and soy-based seasonings on each piece; ebi-mayo.
osaka_sushi_shizuku_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fish, shellfish and sea urchin throughout; chawanmushi.
osaka_sushi_shizuku_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon, Tue, Thu–Sun 18:00–23:00 in two seatings, 18:00–20:30 and 21:00–23:00; closed Wed (Tabelog). Reservation needed and hard to get; one diner booked a year ahead (September 2026). Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_sushi_shizuku_shinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · creative sushi with a sauce for every piece, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A ten-seat sushi room on Suomachi-dori, open since 2016, a Tabelog Award Bronze winner in 2025 and 2026 and so hard to book that one diner waited a year. It breaks from Edomae: each piece comes with its own house sauce or condiments and hidden knife work, like aori squid scored so finely it turns fluffy, topped with sea urchin. The ¥22,000 course might open with grilled kuruma shrimp under karasumi, run through flounder, yuzu-scented sea bream and a sweet potato chawanmushi, then grilled mackerel with ume and condiments, tuna and anago. Save room for the add-ons: a toro-taku roll and an "adult" ebi-mayo one diner calls a must, though one diner found the ¥10,000 uni hand roll and the overall bill steep, and the extras not offered clearly. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Creative sushi restaurant; Tabelog Award Bronze 2025 and 2026; Tabelog Sushi WEST 100, 2021, 2022 and 2025 (Tabelog; official site sushi-shizuku.com).
chef_bio.philosophy: Original sauces and condiments matched to each ingredient, with hidden knife techniques (September 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "This restaurant offers a unique take on sushi that differs from traditional Edomae style… original sauces and condiments tailored to each ingredient, incorporating various hidden knife techniques." — September 2026.
"The intricate knife work was visually impressive, and once in my mouth, it was so fluffy that it hardly felt like squid." — October 2026, aori ika.

osaka_uoshige_nishi_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: tuna is the dish; quail egg yolk; miso soup.
osaka_uoshige_nishi_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Tue–Sat 11:30–20:00; closed Mon, Sun and public holidays; closes when sold out; hours may change (Tabelog). Full from opening, but turnover is quick, usually seated within 15 minutes (April 2026). Run by two people (October 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_uoshige_nishi_shinsaibashi.notes: [Rice bowl · ten slices of marinated tuna for ¥1,100 in Nishi-Shinsaibashi] A six-seat wooden counter tucked at the back of a building near Shinsaibashi, run by two people and serving essentially one thing: tekka-don. Ten slices of lean tuna, marinated in a sesame-scented soy sauce, are fanned over warm rice and shredded nori with a quail egg yolk and wasabi in the middle, ¥1,100 with red miso soup and pickles; seven slices are ¥900. On Thursday and Friday it switches to a melting chutoro version. One diner has come for 27 years. The sauce comes already on and runs a little strong for one diner, and the rice is soft. It fills at opening but turns over fast, and it closes when the tuna runs out, so go early. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Tekka-don specialist run by two people (October 2026 review; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "On top of warm rice is a generous amount of shredded nori. On top of that, 10 slices of marinated red meat tuna are lavishly arranged. In the center, there's a quail egg yolk and wasabi." — August 2026, 10 slices ¥1,100; a 27-year customer.

"A limited-time medium fatty tuna rice bowl available only on Thursdays and Fridays. It features ten luxurious slices of medium fatty tuna… The sesame-flavored soy sauce enhances the overall richness." — May 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: 魚重、大阪市中央区西心斎橋1-4-17 シゲタニビル 1F、心斎橋から250m、火〜土 11:30〜20:00、月・日・祝休み(2019年11月から祝日休み)、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター6席。口コミ(2026年4〜10月): 鉄火丼の専門店、7枚900円、7枚ご飯大盛り1,000円、10枚1,100円、10枚ご飯大盛り1,200円、27年通う人、ビルの奥、心斎橋駅7番出口から徒歩3分、木のカウンター、赤だし(わかめ)、香の物(しば漬け、白菜の浅漬け)、温かいご飯に刻み海苔、漬けの赤身10枚、うずらの卵黄とわさび、秘伝のたれ、胡麻の香り、木・金は中トロの鉄火丼、開店から満席でも回転が早く15分ほどで入れる、たれがかかった状態で出てくる、たれが濃く塩辛めという声、ご飯は柔らかめ、清潔、感じのいい接客、二人で営業、なくなり次第終了なので早めに。

osaka_ganso_ice_dog_amemura.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the soft serve is served inside a fried wheat bun.
osaka_ganso_ice_dog_amemura.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–21:00; closing days vary (Tabelog). A short line can form (October 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_ganso_ice_dog_amemura.notes: [Sweets · the original Ice Dog by Triangle Park in Amemura] A small snack shop next to Amemura's Triangle Park, selling the neighborhood's signature street sweet, the Ice Dog: a bun fried to order, crisp outside and fluffy inside, split and stuffed with cold, rich soft serve. The hot-and-cold contrast is the point; eat it quickly before the ice cream melts. Choose vanilla, chocolate or mixed. Opinions vary from "incredibly delicious" to just average, and one diner found ¥700 for a mixed soft serve steep, but it's a fun, cheap Amemura stop and easy to eat walking. Open 11:00 to 21:00. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ice Dog stand in Amerikamura (official site ice-dog.net; Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "It features cold ice cream stuffed in a warm, freshly fried bun, creating an interesting combination of hot and cold. It's perfect for eating on the go." — August 2026.
"The bread was crispy and fluffy, and the soft serve had a gentle sweetness that paired perfectly with it." — October 2026.

osaka_mukaino_gohachi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: tare on the chicken; sauce-soaked grilled rice balls.
osaka_mukaino_gohachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken course; tsukune with quail egg and cheese.
osaka_mukaino_gohachi.hours_raw: From 18:00; closing days vary; hours may change (Tabelog). Reservation only, same-day bookings accepted; seat-only bookings not accepted (Tabelog). Course ¥3,500, drinks ¥400–700 (Tabelog). Often run by one person, so drinks can be slow when full (July 2026). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_mukaino_gohachi.notes: [Yakitori · ¥3,500 chicken course grilled on a teppan in front of you, Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A quiet twelve-seat counter on the third floor of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, open since 2020, where chicken is grilled not over charcoal but on an iron plate at your place, then served with three sauces and salt. There's one ¥3,500 course: appetizers, assorted chicken cuts, a tsukune with cheese and quail egg, and a finale of grilled rice balls, crisp outside and soaked in sauce, which diners single out. Add a potato salad, and drinks run ¥400–700, so the night comes to about ¥4,000–6,000. The cook often works alone, so on a full night drinks can be slow and one diner found the cook too busy to talk. Reservation only, same day is fine. Cash only. The sign is easy to miss.

chef_bio.background: Chicken restaurant, often run by one person (July 2026 review; Tabelog).
chef_bio.specialty: Teppan-grilled chicken course; grilled rice balls.

anecdotes.text: "Mukaino Gohachi is a place where the chef grills yakitori right in front of you using an iron grill… The yakitori is delicious, but the crispy grilled rice balls soaked in flavor for the finish are truly exceptional." — September 2026.
"All the chicken dishes were great, but my personal favorites were the tsukune (meatballs) topped with cheese and quail eggs, as well as the grilled rice balls." — May 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ: むかいの 五八、大阪市中央区東心斎橋1-6-23 清水町会館 3F、長堀橋駅から徒歩4分、18:00〜、不定休、完全予約制(当日予約可、席のみの予約不可)、焼き鳥コース3,500円、ドリンク400〜700円、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター12席、2020年10月1日開店。口コミ(2026年4〜9月): ビルの静かな一角の隠れ家、素材を生かしたシンプルな味付け、店主が話しやすい、チーズとうずらのつくね、焼きおにぎり、看板が見にくい、エレベーターを降りて左、コースのみ、食べるペースを見て焼く、ポテトサラダ、ドリンクが手頃、グループごとに鉄板で焼く、満席の日は一人で営業で飲み物が遅い、量が多い、向かいのビルに五八、鉄板で焼く焼き鳥、3種のたれと塩、一人約4,000円、2名から(未確認という声)。

osaka_iketako_sarunokoshikake.hours_raw: Daily 17:00–24:00 (Tabelog); closed Mondays in September 2026. Takeaway of leftovers, ¥100 packaging (February 2026). Cards, IC cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_iketako_sarunokoshikake.notes: [Izakaya · live octopus a dozen ways, on a 7th floor by Shinsaibashi] A calm, hidden izakaya on the seventh floor of a building two minutes from Shinsaibashi, open since 2020 and devoted to live octopus, mainly from Akashi. It's rare to find octopus treated this many ways: firm, sweet sashimi; octopus shabu-shabu, sliced thin and swished briefly in broth (the dish to try); grilled octopus; octopus kimchi and yukhoe; and takoyaki and Akashiyaki made with live octopus, which have a different texture from the usual. Finish with the octopus rice or an octopus-dashi chazuke. A whole-octopus course lets you choose from the day's preparations, and portions are generous enough that leftovers can be packed to go. Service is warm. Open until midnight. Cards and QR accepted.
